## Scope, independence, and interpretation

This report reconstructs the engineering properties that survive after tracing operations research, management science, decision analysis, queueing, inventory/capacity theory, scheduling, mathematical optimisation, simulation, stochastic and robust optimisation, sequential/online decision methods, multi-criteria analysis, data-driven optimisation and implementation criticism. The analytical label does **not** assert that one historical methodology with this name existed.

The lane was conducted as independent external research. No repository, target implementation, or sibling “Evolved” packet was inspected or used. Source-established relationships with statistics, economics, systems analysis, control, industrial engineering and other traditions are recorded without importing another lane’s synthesis.

## Executive synthesis

The evidence supports the proposed hypothesis, with important qualifications. Once branding and tool ritual are stripped away, the strongest surviving discipline is not “optimise everything”. It is a decision-and-operations engineering practice that first establishes the real consequence, owner, deadline, alternatives, constraints and implementation authority; then represents scarce resources, dependencies, queues, variability and uncertainty only to the fidelity required to discriminate action; preserves recourse, reversibility and near-optimal options when the model cannot justify a unique commitment; validates model and simulation claims against their use domain; recomputes when state changes; monitors realised consequences and gaming; and stops analysis when another result cannot change action enough to justify its cost. [S005–S007, S039–S040, S049, S070, S073–S076, S084–S103]

The mature form is plural. Queueing and teletraffic contribute the capacity–variability–delay relation; inventory and real-options traditions contribute conditional buffer and flexibility value; programming contributes explicit feasible alternatives and scarcity; scheduling contributes precedence/resource/current-state logic; decision analysis contributes consequences, preferences and information value; stochastic/robust methods contribute differentiated uncertainty and recourse; simulation contributes controlled counterfactual evidence under bounded credibility; and modern online/data-driven methods contribute adaptive policies while inheriting stronger shift, feedback and deployment burdens. [S001–S041, S050–S069, S084–S097, S112–S121]

Criticism changes the final property population materially. Expected utility is normatively useful but descriptively incomplete; weighted scores expose judgement without objectifying it; solver optimality is model-relative; utilisation targets can induce congestion; deterministic schedules drift; more simulation runs do not cure model-form error; robust optimisation can be over-conservative; forecasts can be accurate yet decision-poor; deployed models change behaviour and data; and technically superior recommendations can fail because authority, incentives, local knowledge or maintenance are absent. These are not “wrong solver” problems. [S043–S046, S070, S078–S080, S088–S110]

## Research method and saturation stop rule

Research proceeded across independent lineages and criticism families rather than around a predetermined property list. Historical primary sources and monographs established genealogy; mathematical papers established formal mechanisms and assumption boundaries; current reviews and engineering guidance established present practice; empirical and implementation studies tested transfer; and critical sources were used to reject or narrow claims. Searches continued through current-year material on DRO, decision-focused learning, online scheduling, queueing for modern compute/LLM systems, simulation uncertainty, maintenance, AI–OR integration and the practice gap.

Saturation was reached when additional searches produced (a) already represented mechanism families, (b) solver variants without a distinct transferable failure-prevention mechanism, or (c) domain applications whose distinct assumptions were already captured. One property remains `UNRESOLVED`: universal quantitative transfer of classical queue/inventory/scheduling formulas to heterogeneous knowledge or agent work. It is frozen as unresolved because the qualitative congestion/dependency mechanisms transfer, while the required stochastic/service abstractions remain empirically unsettled.

Mathematical validity is reported separately from empirical or field validity. A theorem, optimality certificate, convergence result, regret bound or ambiguity guarantee is evidence about a model under assumptions; it is not evidence that the objective, distribution, uncertainty set, state, service process, human authority or implementation fits a real system. Current preprints and frontier papers are used to establish active research direction, not mature field payoff.

## Tested candidate description

> **Frozen candidate description.** `EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING` is an engineering discipline that frames the real decision before modelling it; generates and preserves meaningful alternatives; makes consequences, objectives, constraints, uncertainty, resource conflicts, dependencies, queues and recourse explicit; uses optimisation, scheduling, forecasting and simulation only at decision-requisite fidelity; tests sensitivity, robustness, currentness and implementation authority; adapts when state changes; monitors realised consequences and proxy capture; stops analysis when marginal decision value no longer justifies delay or cost; and prefers a cheap authoritative discriminator or simple policy whenever added complexity cannot change action materially.

This description is retained because it is supported across the plural genealogy and survives the criticism record. It is not a claim that every property triggers in every domain, nor that one solver, formula, scorecard, schedule, simulation, AI method or named process is required.

| “More simulation runs mean more truth.” | OPTIMISATION_OR_SCHEDULING_CEREMONY / SIMULATION_MODEL | More independent replications reduce Monte Carlo error only. They do not fix wrong inputs, transients, dependence, structural error or invalid decision use. | [P050, P051, P061] | [S084, S085, S086, S087, S088, S089] |
| “If the model is solved optimally, the engineering problem is solved.” | ALGORITHM_OR_SOLVER_TECHNIQUE vs REAL_DEPLOYED_PRACTICE | Formulation, objective validity, externalities, uncertainty, authority, implementability and monitoring survive solver completion. | [P006, P015, P018, P019, P055] | [S070, S089, S098, S101, S102] |
| “Slack is waste.” | METRIC_OR_OBJECTIVE_CAPTURE | Slack, reserve and inventory have both cost and option/recovery value; their warranted level depends on variability, coupling, shortage consequence and lead time. | [P009, P025, P035, P036] | [S003, S004, S057, S058, S059] |
| “Queues are operational noise rather than system behaviour.” | QUEUE_OR_CAPACITY_MODEL | Queues are an observable consequence of arrival, service, routing, variability, admission and bottleneck structure, including hidden work and retries. | [P021, P023, P027, P028] | [S001, S014, S015, S052, S055] |
| “Robustness means choose the most conservative solution.” | TEXTBOOK_SIMPLIFICATION / UNCERTAINTY_MODEL | Mature robustness calibrates an uncertainty or ambiguity set, exposes the price of protection and preserves recourse; blanket worst case can be wasteful. | [P042, P044, P045] | [S023, S024, S025, S026, S033] |
| “More parallel workers always shorten completion time.” | SCHEDULING_MODEL / QUEUE_OR_CAPACITY_MODEL | Parallelism helps only when precedence, shared resources, acceptance capacity, coordination and bottleneck structure permit it. | [P024, P028, P029, P034] | [S009, S014, S017, S061, S062] |
| “A better prediction metric means a better operational policy.” | DATA_DRIVEN_OPTIMISATION_TRANSLATION | Prediction and decision losses differ; optimisation can amplify errors and deployment can change the population being predicted. | [P017, P046, P054, P055] | [S067, S068, S069, S096, S097] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY_LEDGER
The frozen denominator contains **66 properties/candidates**, including retained, context-dependent, assumption-sensitive, domain-specific, superseded, rejected, ceremonial and unresolved dispositions. No candidate is silently dropped. The machine-readable ledger contains the same population and fields.

### P001 — Explicit decision owner, consumer, deadline, and action authority
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONVERGENT_PROPERTY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Wartime operational research's mission-facing teams; post-war decision analysis and systems analysis; current NASA/DoD trade-study guidance. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | OR analysts were attached to an operation and decision command; decision analysis later made the decision maker and action explicit. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Technically elaborate analysis can be produced without anyone authorised to choose, implement, or bear consequences. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | A model, dashboard, or recommendation has no live decision consumer, no deadline, or ambiguous authority, so analysis cannot control action legitimately. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | A model, dashboard, or recommendation has no live decision consumer, no deadline, or ambiguous authority, so analysis cannot control action legitimately. |
| MECHANISM | Record the named owner, implementers, deadline/review point, escalation and override authority, and the action the evidence can change. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Any consequential allocation, schedule, optimisation, trade study, forecast-controlled action, or automated policy. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | For low-consequence reversible choices, name one accountable chooser and a decision time; no formal charter is required. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A named person or body must own the decision, be able to accept consequences, and have a deadline or review point. Analysts and solvers are not authority by default. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The valued consequence, decision criteria, hard constraints, soft preferences, and non-compensatory limits must be distinguishable and challengeable. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Only information capable of discriminating alternatives is required on the cheap path; provenance, timing, and material omissions must be known when formal analysis is used. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The represented alternatives and consequences span the live decision sufficiently for the claimed conclusion; framing and elicitation are not neutral facts. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Material ambiguity about consequences, preferences, feasibility, timing, or future information is stated rather than silently converted to precise inputs. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | The resources needed to analyse and implement each alternative are included where they can change feasibility or ranking. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Fewer category errors, fewer dominated or infeasible commitments, and a traceable basis for choosing, deferring, escalating, or preserving options. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The accountable decision owner and implementers who must act on the result. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Omitted alternatives, inherited framing, false precision, authority gaps, post-hoc criteria changes, and a model with no live decision consumer. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Decision analysis can be normatively coherent while elicited preferences are unstable or stakeholders disagree; explicitness does not make values objective. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Command/client attachment evolved into explicit decision ownership, governance, human-in-the-loop authority, and model-maintenance responsibility. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Analysis begins with an owner-action-deadline tuple and ends in an implementable choice, deferment, experiment, policy, or documented non-decision. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A steering committee, sign-off sheet, or RACI is optional; an accountable consequence-bearing authority is not. |

### P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | MATHEMATICAL_PROGRAMMING_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | MATHEMATICAL_PROGRAMMING_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Linear and integer programming, analysis of alternatives, constrained scheduling and current engineering trade-study guidance. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Define a feasible region with resource and technical constraints; use integrality where actions are discrete. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A modelled limit may be a preference, an unenforceable aspiration, or an omitted real constraint. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | The solver returns a mathematically feasible but operationally impossible recommendation, or trades through a genuinely hard limit via a penalty. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | The solver returns a mathematically feasible but operationally impossible recommendation, or trades through a genuinely hard limit via a penalty. |
| MECHANISM | Classify constraints by source, owner, enforceability, uncertainty and violation consequence; test feasibility against implementation conditions and preserve veto/lexicographic limits where compensation is illegitimate. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Any optimisation, schedule, allocation or scored trade study with limits or prerequisites. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use direct admissibility screening before scoring; a hard authoritative discriminator can end the comparison. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A named person or body must own the decision, be able to accept consequences, and have a deadline or review point. Analysts and solvers are not authority by default. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The valued consequence, decision criteria, hard constraints, soft preferences, and non-compensatory limits must be distinguishable and challengeable. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Only information capable of discriminating alternatives is required on the cheap path; provenance, timing, and material omissions must be known when formal analysis is used. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The represented alternatives and consequences span the live decision sufficiently for the claimed conclusion; framing and elicitation are not neutral facts. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Material ambiguity about consequences, preferences, feasibility, timing, or future information is stated rather than silently converted to precise inputs. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | The resources needed to analyse and implement each alternative are included where they can change feasibility or ranking. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Fewer category errors, fewer dominated or infeasible commitments, and a traceable basis for choosing, deferring, escalating, or preserving options. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The accountable decision owner and implementers who must act on the result. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Omitted alternatives, inherited framing, false precision, authority gaps, post-hoc criteria changes, and a model with no live decision consumer. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Decision analysis can be normatively coherent while elicited preferences are unstable or stakeholders disagree; explicitness does not make values objective. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Pure algebraic feasibility evolved toward mixed hard/soft, chance/robust, implementation and policy constraints with explicit slack semantics. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Constraint status is challengeable and linked to enforcement, uncertainty, recourse and violation consequence; infeasibility is diagnostic, not proof that reality is impossible. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A solver constraint row is not the property; truthful admissibility and enforceability are. |

| FIELD_OR_OPERATIONAL_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH | LOW |
| IMPLEMENTATION_CASE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH | MODERATE |
| TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY | MODERATE |
| CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH | MODERATE |

### P006 — Trace objectives to consequences and resist proxy substitution
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | STRONGLY_RETAINED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONVERGENT_PROPERTY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Operational objectives in early OR; utility/loss modelling; Goodhart/Campbell critiques; modern algorithmic-bias and model-governance evidence. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Optimise an explicit operational objective or expected utility. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A measurable target replaces the actual outcome and changes behaviour once optimised. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Metric improvement is reported as real improvement despite externalities, displaced cost, hidden queues, selection effects or changed behaviour. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Metric improvement is reported as real improvement despite externalities, displaced cost, hidden queues, selection effects or changed behaviour. |
| MECHANISM | Create a consequence-to-objective trace, identify proxy gaps and affected parties, monitor independent outcomes and distribution shifts, and allow retirement or redesign of captured metrics. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Whenever a KPI, score, forecast loss, utilisation, throughput, service level, or learned reward controls incentives or action. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Where a direct outcome or authoritative constraint is observable, use it instead of a composite proxy. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The owner of the real consequence must be distinct from owners rewarded on the proxy, with authority to audit and revise measures. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Proxy, target, constraint, distributional impact, externalities, and opportunities for reclassification or cost shifting are explicit. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Metric provenance, denominators, missingness, threshold behaviour, classification changes, and outcome measures independent of the target are monitored. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The proxy remains causally and institutionally linked to the valued outcome after it becomes a target. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Strategic adaptation and feedback-induced distribution shift are expected rather than treated as noise. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Independent outcome measurement, audit capacity, metric rotation or retirement, and exception review are funded. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Lower probability that optimisation improves the dashboard while degrading the system or shifting harm outside the model boundary. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The consequence owner, affected stakeholders, and governance authority—not only the metric-producing unit. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Threshold gaming, queue hiding, backlog reclassification, schedule padding, cost shifting, dropped constraints, selective scenarios, and post-hoc weights. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Anti-gaming controls themselves can create complexity and new gaming surfaces; the mature form prefers direct consequences and plural indicators where feasible. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Single operational objectives evolved toward multi-objective, fairness/externality constraints, causal monitoring and performative-feedback awareness. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | A proxy remains provisional evidence about a consequence, with independent outcome validation and an explicit gaming/feedback model. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | An objective function or dashboard is optional; objective–consequence validity is the property. |

### P007 — Preserve multiple objectives, Pareto structure, and non-compensatory limits
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | MULTI_CRITERIA_DECISION_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | HYBRID_RESOLUTION |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Multi-attribute utility, vector optimisation, Pareto efficiency, outranking and modern multi-objective optimisation. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Represent several valued attributes and their preference trade-offs or efficient frontier. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A single weighted objective hides conflict, permits illegitimate compensation, or presents one preference choice as mathematically necessary. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Aggregate score improves while a critical criterion, stakeholder, tail consequence or hard threshold worsens unacceptably. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Aggregate score improves while a critical criterion, stakeholder, tail consequence or hard threshold worsens unacceptably. |
| MECHANISM | Use dominance/Pareto screening, thresholds/vetoes or lexicographic rules, expose scalarisation assumptions, and show efficient/near-efficient alternatives rather than only one score. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Decisions with genuinely conflicting consequences, stakeholder values, quality attributes or fairness/efficiency tensions. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use a small consequence table and dominance check; do not aggregate when one alternative clearly dominates or a hard threshold decides. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A legitimate decision owner and affected stakeholders must own criteria, thresholds, weights, vetoes, and aggregation rules. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Criteria meanings, scale type, non-compensatory limits, stakeholder conflicts, and uncertainty are explicit; a total score is not presumed to be value truth. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Alternative performance evidence, scale definitions, normalisation rules, weights or preference statements, and uncertainty ranges are traceable. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Preferential/utility independence, cardinality, compensability, commensurability, and aggregation-method assumptions are explicit. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Weight, score, threshold, normalisation, and alternative-set sensitivity are analysed where they could change ranking or admissibility. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Elicitation, facilitation, dispute resolution, data collection, and sensitivity analysis costs are proportionate to consequence. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Transparent, challengeable trade-offs and preservation of Pareto, veto, and stakeholder information that a single proxy would erase. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The accountable owner and stakeholders whose values are represented or whose disagreement is preserved. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Rank reversal, arbitrary normalisation, false cardinal arithmetic on ordinal scores, compensating across hard limits, post-hoc weights, and spreadsheet objectivity theatre. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Different MCDA methods embody different value models and can rank the same alternatives differently; explicit judgement is not eliminated by arithmetic. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Weighted utility evolved into Pareto sets, outranking, non-compensatory rules, interactive elicitation and sensitivity analysis. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Conflict remains visible; aggregation is an owned preference model, not objective truth, and alternative rankings are tested across plausible preferences. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A weighted matrix is optional and often inferior; explicit trade-offs and admissibility are the property. |

### P009 — Account for reversibility, irreversibility, option value, and staged commitment

| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | An irreversible action is taken too early, or a reversible low-cost experiment is over-analysed as though it were final commitment. |
| MECHANISM | Classify reversibility, lock-in, expiry, switching/rollback cost, learning opportunities and staged gates; price formally only where inputs support it. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Capital commitments, architecture lock-in, contracts, irreversible external actions, long-lived capacity and uncertain technology choices. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use qualitative option-preservation and reversibility screening for small or poorly quantified decisions. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |

| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Only information capable of discriminating alternatives is required on the cheap path; provenance, timing, and material omissions must be known when formal analysis is used. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The represented alternatives and consequences span the live decision sufficiently for the claimed conclusion; framing and elicitation are not neutral facts. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Material ambiguity about consequences, preferences, feasibility, timing, or future information is stated rather than silently converted to precise inputs. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | The resources needed to analyse and implement each alternative are included where they can change feasibility or ranking. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Fewer category errors, fewer dominated or infeasible commitments, and a traceable basis for choosing, deferring, escalating, or preserving options. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The accountable decision owner and implementers who must act on the result. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Omitted alternatives, inherited framing, false precision, authority gaps, post-hoc criteria changes, and a model with no live decision consumer. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Decision analysis can be normatively coherent while elicited preferences are unstable or stakeholders disagree; explicitness does not make values objective. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Financial real-options models broadened into staged experiments, pilots, modular commitments and explicit rollback/exit criteria. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Decision depth and commitment scale are proportional to irreversibility; reversible options can be exercised cheaply while irreversible choices preserve learning value. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Black–Scholes-style valuation is not general; explicit commitment and learning structure is. |

### P010 — Represent decision horizon, dependencies, and sequential coupling
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | SEQUENTIAL_OR_ONLINE_DECISION_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONTROL_THEORY_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Dynamic programming, Markov decision processes, sequential inventory and decision-tree traditions. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Choose a policy over states and stages rather than an isolated action. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A locally attractive action changes future state, information, capacity, or available alternatives. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Myopic optimisation improves the current step while degrading future feasibility, option value, queues or total cost. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Myopic optimisation improves the current step while degrading future feasibility, option value, queues or total cost. |
| MECHANISM | Identify state, stage, dependency, future information, transition, terminal consequence and commitment; use a simple look-ahead or formal dynamic model as warranted. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Linked decisions, replenishment, scheduling, capacity investment, maintenance, adaptive policies and any action with material carry-over effects. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use an explicit two-step consequence/dependency check when full dynamic programming is disproportionate. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A named person or body must own the decision, be able to accept consequences, and have a deadline or review point. Analysts and solvers are not authority by default. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The valued consequence, decision criteria, hard constraints, soft preferences, and non-compensatory limits must be distinguishable and challengeable. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Only information capable of discriminating alternatives is required on the cheap path; provenance, timing, and material omissions must be known when formal analysis is used. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The represented alternatives and consequences span the live decision sufficiently for the claimed conclusion; framing and elicitation are not neutral facts. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Material ambiguity about consequences, preferences, feasibility, timing, or future information is stated rather than silently converted to precise inputs. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | The resources needed to analyse and implement each alternative are included where they can change feasibility or ranking. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Fewer category errors, fewer dominated or infeasible commitments, and a traceable basis for choosing, deferring, escalating, or preserving options. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The accountable decision owner and implementers who must act on the result. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Omitted alternatives, inherited framing, false precision, authority gaps, post-hoc criteria changes, and a model with no live decision consumer. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Decision analysis can be normatively coherent while elicited preferences are unstable or stakeholders disagree; explicitness does not make values objective. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Finite-stage dynamic programming evolved toward MDPs, approximate/online methods, receding horizons and policy-based operation. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | The unit of decision is a state-contingent policy or staged commitment when future coupling matters, not a falsely independent one-shot optimum. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A Bellman recursion is optional; representing material future-state effects is the property. |

### P011 — Match model fidelity and analysis depth to decision consequence
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | STRONGLY_RETAINED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | HYBRID_RESOLUTION |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Requisite decision modelling, bounded rationality/metareasoning, model-validation practice and NASA decision guidance. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Build only enough model detail for the decision; a model is requisite when further refinement does not materially alter choice. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Detail, precision and integration are mistaken for decision quality. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Analysis costs and delays grow while added fidelity cannot change the next action, or a crude model is used where small errors reverse an irreversible choice. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Analysis costs and delays grow while added fidelity cannot change the next action, or a crude model is used where small errors reverse an irreversible choice. |
| MECHANISM | Link fidelity to consequence, uncertainty, reversibility and decision sensitivity; test whether refinements can change admissibility or ranking. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Any choice of modelling depth, simulation detail, data collection, solver exactness or review breadth. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use bounds, dominance, sensitivity or a simple discriminator before building a richer model. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must set the value of delay, error, information, computation, and reversibility; the analyst cannot optimise analysis effort against an unstated consequence model. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The analysis objective is decision improvement, not model detail, run count, document completeness, or solver prestige. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | An estimate—formal or qualitative—of whether another observation, model refinement, scenario, review, or computation could change action. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The current alternative ordering and plausible information effects are represented well enough to judge marginal decision value. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Uncertainty in both the underlying decision and the analysis-value estimate is acknowledged; formal VOI formulas require credible probability and value models. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Time, attention, compute, experiment cost, and opportunity cost are explicit analysis resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | More timely decisions and concentration of scarce analysis effort where it can plausibly alter consequences. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The decision owner who can stop, continue, reopen, or act. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Analysis paralysis, arbitrary deadlines, stopping on fatigue, endless scenario accumulation, or over-formal VOI built on invented probabilities. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Exact value-of-information and metareasoning models are assumption-intensive; a qualitative decision-change test is often the mature cheap path. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Bounded rationality and requisite models converged with value-of-information, validation, and risk-proportionate engineering guidance. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Use the least-cost model that is adequate to discriminate the consequential decision, with a reopen rule when state or sensitivity changes. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A comprehensive model is not inherently mature; decision-relative adequacy is. |

| EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_STRENGTH | MODERATE |
| FIELD_OR_OPERATIONAL_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH | LOW |
| IMPLEMENTATION_CASE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH | MODERATE |
| TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY | MODERATE |

| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Complexity adds latency, maintenance and gaming surfaces without changing action or consequence. |
| MECHANISM | Check hard constraints, dominance, feasibility, obvious bottlenecks, threshold rules and bounded heuristics first; escalate only when residual ambiguity is decision-relevant. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Low-consequence, reversible, time-limited, repeated or structurally simple decisions, and preliminary screening of complex decisions. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | This property is itself the cheap path: apply the least expensive valid discriminator with explicit limits. |

| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The analysis objective is decision improvement, not model detail, run count, document completeness, or solver prestige. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | An estimate—formal or qualitative—of whether another observation, model refinement, scenario, review, or computation could change action. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The current alternative ordering and plausible information effects are represented well enough to judge marginal decision value. |

| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Time, attention, compute, experiment cost, and opportunity cost are explicit analysis resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | More timely decisions and concentration of scarce analysis effort where it can plausibly alter consequences. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The decision owner who can stop, continue, reopen, or act. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Analysis paralysis, arbitrary deadlines, stopping on fatigue, endless scenario accumulation, or over-formal VOI built on invented probabilities. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Exact value-of-information and metareasoning models are assumption-intensive; a qualitative decision-change test is often the mature cheap path. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Satisficing and heuristics evolved into decision-relative model requisiteness, approximation guarantees, metareasoning and learning-augmented fallback policies. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Simple rules are preferred when validated for the context and monitored for drift; complexity is justified by incremental decision value, not prestige. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Neither simplicity nor exact optimisation is a virtue in itself; proportional discrimination is the property. |

### P014 — Use explicit stop and reopen rules tied to possible action change
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | HYBRID_RESOLUTION |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Requisite decision modelling, sequential analysis, value-of-information and rolling decision practice. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Stop refining when the model is sufficient for choice; update when new information changes the decision state. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Analysis stops arbitrarily, continues ceremonially, or is never reopened after the state invalidates it. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Either analysis paralysis or stale decisions persist despite decision-changing evidence. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Either analysis paralysis or stale decisions persist despite decision-changing evidence. |
| MECHANISM | Define stop criteria using stability of admissibility/ranking under plausible changes, remaining VOI and deadline; define reopen triggers for material state, objective, constraint, evidence or authority change. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Any iterative analysis, model review, schedule, forecast, allocation policy or decision-support system. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | A verbal rule can suffice: stop when the next evidence cannot change action enough; reopen when it can. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must set the value of delay, error, information, computation, and reversibility; the analyst cannot optimise analysis effort against an unstated consequence model. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The analysis objective is decision improvement, not model detail, run count, document completeness, or solver prestige. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | An estimate—formal or qualitative—of whether another observation, model refinement, scenario, review, or computation could change action. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The current alternative ordering and plausible information effects are represented well enough to judge marginal decision value. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Uncertainty in both the underlying decision and the analysis-value estimate is acknowledged; formal VOI formulas require credible probability and value models. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Time, attention, compute, experiment cost, and opportunity cost are explicit analysis resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | More timely decisions and concentration of scarce analysis effort where it can plausibly alter consequences. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The decision owner who can stop, continue, reopen, or act. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Analysis paralysis, arbitrary deadlines, stopping on fatigue, endless scenario accumulation, or over-formal VOI built on invented probabilities. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Exact value-of-information and metareasoning models are assumption-intensive; a qualitative decision-change test is often the mature cheap path. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Model requisiteness and sequential decision rules converged with continuous monitoring and rolling re-optimisation. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Closure is conditional and evidence-bound, not permanent; re-analysis is event-triggered rather than calendar ritual. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A fixed review cadence can support but does not replace decision-changing triggers. |

| FIELD_OR_OPERATIONAL_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH | LOW |
| IMPLEMENTATION_CASE_STRENGTH | HIGH |

| TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH | HIGH |

### P015 — State model assumptions and validity domain as part of the decision claim
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | STRONGLY_RETAINED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONVERGENT_PROPERTY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Mathematical programming, queueing, simulation validation, stochastic/robust optimisation and model-criticism traditions. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Mathematical conclusions are conditional on model axioms, distributions, feasible sets and data. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A theorem or solver result is presented without the assumptions that make it relevant to the real operation. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | A valid calculation is transferred outside its stationarity, independence, causal, behavioural, distributional, or implementation domain. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | A valid calculation is transferred outside its stationarity, independence, causal, behavioural, distributional, or implementation domain. |
| MECHANISM | Attach an assumption register and validity boundary to each material recommendation; test high-leverage assumptions through sensitivity, validation, stress or field evidence. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Any formal model, simulation, forecast, queue formula, scorecard, optimisation or learned policy. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | List only assumptions capable of changing action; use a direct caveat and fallback when validation is infeasible. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must approve the represented objective, constraints, alternatives, tolerances, and implementation rules; solver output is advice unless authority is explicitly automated. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The mathematical objective is traceable to valued consequences; hard constraints are enforceable; penalties, scaling, and proxies are challengeable. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Coefficients, feasible sets, capacities, costs, forecasts, and current state have provenance and uncertainty appropriate to their leverage on the solution. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Functional form, linearity/convexity, integrality, independence, horizon, decomposition, and numerical tolerances are stated and tested where material. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Sensitivity, out-of-sample performance, scenario or ambiguity analysis, and model-form uncertainty are addressed according to consequence. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Formulation, solve time, compute, data maintenance, implementation effort, and switching/reconfiguration costs are part of the decision. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Transparent resource trade-offs and high-value improvements in complex feasible spaces where simpler discrimination is inadequate. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of the allocation, design, policy, or schedule and the operators who must implement it. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Optimising the wrong objective, infeasible or unenforceable constraints, numerical false precision, brittle point estimates, local optimum/global harm, and solver optimality worship. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Formal optimality is conditional on the model; small optimality gaps can coexist with large real-world regret, and more exact algorithms do not repair misspecification. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Method-specific assumptions evolved into model-risk, validation-domain, uncertainty-set and out-of-sample governance. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Claims are scoped: optimal/valid under a stated representation and current evidence, with explicit transfer and drift limits. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A generic limitations section is insufficient; assumptions must be linked to decision sensitivity. |

### P017 — Correct for optimiser's curse and validate out-of-sample decision performance
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |

| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Decision-analysis optimiser's curse, statistical estimation risk, stochastic-program value comparisons and modern predict-then-optimise research. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Selecting the maximum estimated value induces upward bias and post-decision disappointment. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | The optimiser preferentially selects alternatives whose estimated inputs contain favourable error. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | In-sample or point-estimate optimum underperforms after deployment even when the estimation method is unbiased marginally. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | In-sample or point-estimate optimum underperforms after deployment even when the estimation method is unbiased marginally. |
| MECHANISM | Use shrinkage/Bayesian adjustment where justified, cross-validation or held-out decision loss, scenario/robust analysis, post-decision calibration and comparison to simple baselines. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Many alternatives, noisy estimated values, flexible models, data-driven objectives, close options or repeated model tuning. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Apply a winner's-curse caution, confidence interval and simple baseline comparison before elaborate correction. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must approve the represented objective, constraints, alternatives, tolerances, and implementation rules; solver output is advice unless authority is explicitly automated. |

| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Coefficients, feasible sets, capacities, costs, forecasts, and current state have provenance and uncertainty appropriate to their leverage on the solution. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Functional form, linearity/convexity, integrality, independence, horizon, decomposition, and numerical tolerances are stated and tested where material. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Sensitivity, out-of-sample performance, scenario or ambiguity analysis, and model-form uncertainty are addressed according to consequence. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Formulation, solve time, compute, data maintenance, implementation effort, and switching/reconfiguration costs are part of the decision. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Transparent resource trade-offs and high-value improvements in complex feasible spaces where simpler discrimination is inadequate. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of the allocation, design, policy, or schedule and the operators who must implement it. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Optimising the wrong objective, infeasible or unenforceable constraints, numerical false precision, brittle point estimates, local optimum/global harm, and solver optimality worship. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Formal optimality is conditional on the model; small optimality gaps can coexist with large real-world regret, and more exact algorithms do not repair misspecification. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Decision-analysis bias correction expanded into out-of-sample prescription evaluation, robust/data-driven optimisation and post-deployment monitoring. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Recommendation evidence includes expected out-of-sample consequence and uncertainty, not only best fitted objective. |

### P019 — Establish implementation feasibility, operational authority, and usable decision support
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | STRONGLY_RETAINED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | INDUSTRIAL_ENGINEERING_HYBRID |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | OR implementation studies, problem-structuring methods, decision conferencing, engineering trade guidance and human–algorithm research. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Deliver recommendations to managers/operators for implementation. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | The mathematically preferred action conflicts with authority, workflow, incentives, local knowledge, explanation needs or integration constraints. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | The recommendation is ignored, selectively followed, worked around, or causes hidden operational damage. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | The recommendation is ignored, selectively followed, worked around, or causes hidden operational damage. |
| MECHANISM | Co-design constraints and exceptions with operators, identify decision/override rights, test workflow and data latency, expose sensitivities, plan fallback, and measure implementation costs. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Any recommendation requiring organisational behaviour, software integration, recurring operator use, or automated enforcement. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | For one-off simple decisions, verify authority, resource availability and direct executability with the responsible operator. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The operational authority, data owner, model owner, affected users, and override/escalation rights must be explicit. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The implementable consequence, not mathematical recommendation alone, is the success criterion. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Live data freshness, local constraints, exceptions, incentives, override behaviour, and post-decision outcomes are observable. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Operators can execute the recommendation, incentives do not systematically defeat it, and the model remains current after deployment. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Human adaptation, workarounds, changing incentives, trust calibration, and organisational drift are treated as model uncertainty. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Training, integration, change effort, exception handling, maintenance, and feedback capacity are included. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Recommendations that survive contact with authority, workflow, incentives, data latency, and operator knowledge. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The people or automated systems that act, plus the authority that owns exceptions and consequences. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Technically superior but unusable recommendations, shadow systems, stale models, selective compliance, unowned overrides, and blaming users for revealed model defects. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Adoption is not proof of validity and resistance is not proof of irrationality; implementation can reveal missing constraints or conflicting objectives. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | ‘User acceptance’ framing evolved toward sociotechnical fit, local-knowledge feedback, trust calibration, override governance and model ownership. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Implementation is part of model validity; resistance can be evidence of missing constraints rather than a defect in users. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Change-management activity is not inherently required; operational feasibility and authority are. |

### P021 — Represent demand, arrivals, service, capacity, and variability before capacity claims
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | QUEUEING_AND_TELETRAFFIC_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | QUEUEING_OR_INVENTORY_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Erlang teletraffic, queueing theory, call-centre/service operations and time-varying queue research. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Relate offered traffic and service capacity to loss or waiting under stochastic arrivals and service. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Capacity is treated as a static average while timing, service variation, retries and routing determine congestion. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Average capacity appears sufficient but bursts or service variability produce long queues, loss, abandonment or missed deadlines. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Average capacity appears sufficient but bursts or service variability produce long queues, loss, abandonment or missed deadlines. |
| MECHANISM | Represent arrival/demand and service/capacity processes at the time scale of the decision; include variability, routing, retrials and finite limits when material. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Shared service systems with stochastic demand, backlogs, latency/service commitments or capacity investment. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Measure arrivals, completions, backlog age, utilisation and peak-to-average behaviour before fitting a parametric queue. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | An operational owner must control or influence capacity, admission, priority, service discipline, demand shaping, or service commitments. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Throughput, waiting, abandonment, service level, tail latency, cost, fairness, and overload consequences must not be collapsed into utilisation alone. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Arrival/demand timing, service-time or capacity behaviour, variability, retries, blocking, priority classes, and backlog/WIP measurements at decision-relevant granularity. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Stationarity, independence, service discipline, routing, finite/infinite buffers, steady-state existence, and workload homogeneity are explicit where formulas rely on them. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Burstiness, nonstationarity, failures, retrials, rare surges, correlated demand, and model-form uncertainty are stress-tested when consequential. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Servers, people, processors, shared acceptance resources, buffers, and surge/reserve capacity are represented as coupled resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Avoided congestion collapse, credible service commitments, visible bottlenecks, and capacity decisions that account for variability and delay. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of staffing, capacity, admission, prioritisation, or service-level policy. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Average-rate fallacy, hidden queues, 100% utilisation targets, steady-state formulas in transient overload, false independence, and adding parallel workers behind a shared bottleneck. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Parametric queue models can be powerful within domain but are brittle under heterogeneous, strategic, nonstationary, or feedback-coupled work; qualitative congestion properties transfer more widely than distributions. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Stationary single-node formulas broadened to many-server, time-varying, network, priority, abandonment and simulation models. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Use the least-assumptive demand/capacity representation that discriminates overload, waiting and reserve decisions, with transient validation. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | M/M/1 notation is optional; representing demand, service and variability is not. |
**Evidence-strength partition**

| Partition | Strength |
| --- | --- |
| HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| FIELD_OR_OPERATIONAL_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| IMPLEMENTATION_CASE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY | HIGH |
| CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| SYNTHESIS_NOTE | Strong universal qualitative property; parametric form remains domain-sensitive. |

### P022 — Govern utilisation jointly with waiting, congestion, and tail performance
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | QUEUEING_AND_TELETRAFFIC_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | QUEUEING_OR_INVENTORY_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Heavy-traffic queueing, many-server staffing, service operations, Factory Physics and large-scale computer systems. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Waiting grows nonlinearly as offered load approaches service capacity under queueing assumptions. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Utilisation is optimised as if idle capacity were pure waste. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Near-100% utilisation creates exploding delay, tail latency, abandonment, brittle recovery and hidden backlog. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Near-100% utilisation creates exploding delay, tail latency, abandonment, brittle recovery and hidden backlog. |
| MECHANISM | Set utilisation/capacity targets from acceptable waiting/tail/service consequences and variability; retain reserve where marginal delay cost justifies it. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Variable demand, finite deadlines, latency-sensitive service, failure/retry loops or expensive queues. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Plot utilisation, queue age and tail delay together; reduce load or add reserve when congestion inflects. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | An operational owner must control or influence capacity, admission, priority, service discipline, demand shaping, or service commitments. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Throughput, waiting, abandonment, service level, tail latency, cost, fairness, and overload consequences must not be collapsed into utilisation alone. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Arrival/demand timing, service-time or capacity behaviour, variability, retries, blocking, priority classes, and backlog/WIP measurements at decision-relevant granularity. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Stationarity, independence, service discipline, routing, finite/infinite buffers, steady-state existence, and workload homogeneity are explicit where formulas rely on them. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Burstiness, nonstationarity, failures, retrials, rare surges, correlated demand, and model-form uncertainty are stress-tested when consequential. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Servers, people, processors, shared acceptance resources, buffers, and surge/reserve capacity are represented as coupled resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Avoided congestion collapse, credible service commitments, visible bottlenecks, and capacity decisions that account for variability and delay. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of staffing, capacity, admission, prioritisation, or service-level policy. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Average-rate fallacy, hidden queues, 100% utilisation targets, steady-state formulas in transient overload, false independence, and adding parallel workers behind a shared bottleneck. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Parametric queue models can be powerful within domain but are brittle under heterogeneous, strategic, nonstationary, or feedback-coupled work; qualitative congestion properties transfer more widely than distributions. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Mean waiting formulas evolved into heavy-traffic, quality-and-efficiency-driven, tail-at-scale and time-varying capacity policies. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Efficiency is assessed at system throughput and service consequence, not maximum busy fraction; controlled idle capacity can be rational. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A fixed ‘safe utilisation’ percentage is not general; the utilisation–delay trade-off is. |

### P023 — Make queues, WIP, backlogs, blocking, and ageing visible
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | QUEUEING_AND_TELETRAFFIC_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | QUEUEING_OR_INVENTORY_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Little's Law, queueing networks, production-flow and service-operations practice. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Relate average number in system, throughput/arrival rate and time in system under stable flow. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Work waiting between stages is absent from dashboards or reclassified, so delay and overload are invisible. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Reported utilisation or completion metrics look healthy while work ages in hidden queues, blocked states, retries or handoffs. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Reported utilisation or completion metrics look healthy while work ages in hidden queues, blocked states, retries or handoffs. |
| MECHANISM | Define queue/WIP states and boundaries; measure arrivals, departures, age, blocked/retry work and flow conservation; reconcile hidden work with throughput and cycle time. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Multi-stage services, workflows, compute pipelines, maintenance, support, review or acceptance bottlenecks. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Count current WIP/backlog by age and stage; apply flow conservation/Little's Law only after boundary and stability checks. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | An operational owner must control or influence capacity, admission, priority, service discipline, demand shaping, or service commitments. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Throughput, waiting, abandonment, service level, tail latency, cost, fairness, and overload consequences must not be collapsed into utilisation alone. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Arrival/demand timing, service-time or capacity behaviour, variability, retries, blocking, priority classes, and backlog/WIP measurements at decision-relevant granularity. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Stationarity, independence, service discipline, routing, finite/infinite buffers, steady-state existence, and workload homogeneity are explicit where formulas rely on them. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Burstiness, nonstationarity, failures, retrials, rare surges, correlated demand, and model-form uncertainty are stress-tested when consequential. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Servers, people, processors, shared acceptance resources, buffers, and surge/reserve capacity are represented as coupled resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Avoided congestion collapse, credible service commitments, visible bottlenecks, and capacity decisions that account for variability and delay. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of staffing, capacity, admission, prioritisation, or service-level policy. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Average-rate fallacy, hidden queues, 100% utilisation targets, steady-state formulas in transient overload, false independence, and adding parallel workers behind a shared bottleneck. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Parametric queue models can be powerful within domain but are brittle under heterogeneous, strategic, nonstationary, or feedback-coupled work; qualitative congestion properties transfer more widely than distributions. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Single queue counts broadened into network flow, WIP-age distributions, retry queues, observability and end-to-end latency. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Waiting work is a first-class system state with explicit ownership, ageing and downstream consequence; dashboards cannot erase queues by classification. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A Kanban board or queue dashboard is optional; complete work-state visibility is the property. |

| ORIGINAL_FORM | Provide trunks, servers or safety stock sufficient for target blocking/service under variable demand. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Slack is treated categorically as waste, or reserve is added without reference to risk and cost. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | System cannot absorb surge, failure, rework or recovery; or excess reserve imposes unjustified cost and hides problems. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | System cannot absorb surge, failure, rework or recovery; or excess reserve imposes unjustified cost and hides problems. |
| MECHANISM | Relate reserve to demand/service variability, tail/service consequence, recovery lead time, common-mode coupling and cost; review after regime change. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Consequential delay/shortage, variable or bursty demand, slow recovery, failure-prone capacity or tightly coupled stages. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use peak/backlog/recovery observations and a bounded reserve rule before fitting a full queue/inventory model. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | An operational owner must control or influence capacity, admission, priority, service discipline, demand shaping, or service commitments. |

| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Stationarity, independence, service discipline, routing, finite/infinite buffers, steady-state existence, and workload homogeneity are explicit where formulas rely on them. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Burstiness, nonstationarity, failures, retrials, rare surges, correlated demand, and model-form uncertainty are stress-tested when consequential. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Servers, people, processors, shared acceptance resources, buffers, and surge/reserve capacity are represented as coupled resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Avoided congestion collapse, credible service commitments, visible bottlenecks, and capacity decisions that account for variability and delay. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of staffing, capacity, admission, prioritisation, or service-level policy. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Average-rate fallacy, hidden queues, 100% utilisation targets, steady-state formulas in transient overload, false independence, and adding parallel workers behind a shared bottleneck. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Parametric queue models can be powerful within domain but are brittle under heterogeneous, strategic, nonstationary, or feedback-coupled work; qualitative congestion properties transfer more widely than distributions. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Fixed safety factors evolved into service-level, many-server, robust/scenario, safety-stock and resilience-aware reserve policies. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Reserve is a priced hedge and recovery option, not waste or virtue; it is conditional, observable and periodically recalibrated. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A universal buffer percentage is rejected; consequence-linked reserve is the property. |

| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Stationary queueing evolved into transient approximations, time-varying networks, autoscaling, admission control and feedback-aware models. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Capacity governance is regime-aware and monitors whether model assumptions and stability conditions currently hold. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A steady-state queue model is not the default; regime classification is the property. |

### P028 — Model queue networks, shared bottlenecks, retries, rework, and blocking when coupled
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | NETWORK_OPTIMISATION_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | QUEUEING_OR_INVENTORY_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Jackson queueing networks, network flow, production systems and large-scale computing/service systems. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Represent routing among several service stations and coupled waiting lines. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A single-stage model ignores downstream blocking, shared acceptance resources, rework loops or retry amplification. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Adding capacity or parallelism at one stage worsens congestion elsewhere or increases total completion time/cost. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Adding capacity or parallelism at one stage worsens congestion elsewhere or increases total completion time/cost. |
| MECHANISM | Map routing, feedback/rework probabilities, shared resources, finite buffers and blocking; evaluate end-to-end throughput and tail consequence. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Pipelines, review/test chains, distributed services, multi-stage maintenance, workflows with rework or common dependencies. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Draw a flow/queue map and identify shared resources/retry loops before using network formulas or simulation. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | An operational owner must control or influence capacity, admission, priority, service discipline, demand shaping, or service commitments. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Throughput, waiting, abandonment, service level, tail latency, cost, fairness, and overload consequences must not be collapsed into utilisation alone. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Arrival/demand timing, service-time or capacity behaviour, variability, retries, blocking, priority classes, and backlog/WIP measurements at decision-relevant granularity. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Stationarity, independence, service discipline, routing, finite/infinite buffers, steady-state existence, and workload homogeneity are explicit where formulas rely on them. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Burstiness, nonstationarity, failures, retrials, rare surges, correlated demand, and model-form uncertainty are stress-tested when consequential. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Servers, people, processors, shared acceptance resources, buffers, and surge/reserve capacity are represented as coupled resources. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Avoided congestion collapse, credible service commitments, visible bottlenecks, and capacity decisions that account for variability and delay. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of staffing, capacity, admission, prioritisation, or service-level policy. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Average-rate fallacy, hidden queues, 100% utilisation targets, steady-state formulas in transient overload, false independence, and adding parallel workers behind a shared bottleneck. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Parametric queue models can be powerful within domain but are brittle under heterogeneous, strategic, nonstationary, or feedback-coupled work; qualitative congestion properties transfer more widely than distributions. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Product-form queue networks broadened into non-product-form, finite-capacity, fork-join, tail, simulation and feedback-control models. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Coupling is represented at enough fidelity to avoid local-capacity and naive-parallelism errors; exact product-form assumptions are not presumed. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A full queueing-network solution is optional; explicit coupling and shared bottlenecks are the property. |

### P029 — Schedule parallel work from real precedence, resource, and acceptance conflicts
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | SCHEDULING_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | SCHEDULING_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | OPERATIONS_RESEARCH_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Multiprocessor/list scheduling, critical-path methods, resource-constrained project scheduling and industrial multi-skill scheduling. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Order activities subject to precedence and machine/resource constraints. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Work is serialised by administrative grouping or parallelised despite hidden resource/test/acceptance conflicts. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Unnecessary delay from false dependencies, or collision/rework from unsafe parallelism. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Unnecessary delay from false dependencies, or collision/rework from unsafe parallelism. |
| MECHANISM | Separate precedence from shared labels; map resource, skill, state, write/acceptance and external conflicts; schedule independent compatible work concurrently. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Multiple ready work units with potential dependency or resource interaction. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Topological plus resource-conflict screening and a simple list/dispatch rule. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A schedule owner must be able to allocate constrained resources, resolve conflicts, change priorities, and re-plan after state changes. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Completion time, tardiness, service, risk, stability, switching/setup cost, resource feasibility, and acceptance constraints are distinguished. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Precedence, release dates, resource/skill needs, setup and blocking conditions, duration uncertainty, deadlines, current progress, and shared validation capacity. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Precedence and resource constraints are real; task durations, preemption, parallelism, calendars, and availability are not treated as certain unless justified. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Breakdowns, rework, duration error, arrivals, resource loss, and changing priorities are represented through buffers, policies, scenarios, or rolling rescheduling as warranted. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Machines, people, skills, processors, test/acceptance channels, external approvals, and switching costs are explicit. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Fewer resource conflicts, less avoidable blocking, earlier completion of genuinely independent work, and controlled adaptation to changed state. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The operational coordinator and resource owners who can execute and revise the schedule. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Confusing shared project labels with dependencies, deterministic critical-path worship, resource-infeasible parallelism, stale published plans, churn from over-reactive replanning, and schedule padding. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Optimal schedules are often fragile to duration and availability error; schedule stability and implementability can dominate nominal makespan. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Deterministic machine scheduling broadened into resource-constrained, multi-skill, multi-project and dynamic execution models. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Parallelism is authorised by current conflict evidence and recomputed after state changes; neither issue-wide serialisation nor maximal concurrency is default. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A Gantt or optimisation solver is optional; truthful dependency/resource boundaries are the property. |

| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Confusing shared project labels with dependencies, deterministic critical-path worship, resource-infeasible parallelism, stale published plans, churn from over-reactive replanning, and schedule padding. |

| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Confusing shared project labels with dependencies, deterministic critical-path worship, resource-infeasible parallelism, stale published plans, churn from over-reactive replanning, and schedule padding. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Optimal schedules are often fragile to duration and availability error; schedule stability and implementability can dominate nominal makespan. |
