### P032 — Recompute schedules and allocations after material state change
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | SCHEDULING_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONTROL_THEORY_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Reactive/dynamic scheduling, rolling-horizon control, time-varying queue staffing and online optimisation. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Monitor execution and reschedule after disruptions or new arrivals. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A schedule is treated as a fixed prediction even after durations, resources, priorities or work state change. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Resources follow a stale critical path or allocation while the actual bottleneck and feasible work have moved. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Resources follow a stale critical path or allocation while the actual bottleneck and feasible work have moved. |
| MECHANISM | Define event and threshold triggers; update current state; recompute feasible ready work and resource allocation; preserve commitments/switching costs where warranted. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Task completion/failure, new work, duration overrun, resource loss, priority/constraint change or observed demand regime shift. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Re-run a simple priority/resource-conflict rule on current state instead of rebuilding a full optimisation. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A schedule owner must be able to allocate constrained resources, resolve conflicts, change priorities, and re-plan after state changes. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Completion time, tardiness, service, risk, stability, switching/setup cost, resource feasibility, and acceptance constraints are distinguished. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Precedence, release dates, resource/skill needs, setup and blocking conditions, duration uncertainty, deadlines, current progress, and shared validation capacity. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Precedence and resource constraints are real; task durations, preemption, parallelism, calendars, and availability are not treated as certain unless justified. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Breakdowns, rework, duration error, arrivals, resource loss, and changing priorities are represented through buffers, policies, scenarios, or rolling rescheduling as warranted. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Machines, people, skills, processors, test/acceptance channels, external approvals, and switching costs are explicit. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Fewer resource conflicts, less avoidable blocking, earlier completion of genuinely independent work, and controlled adaptation to changed state. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The operational coordinator and resource owners who can execute and revise the schedule. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Confusing shared project labels with dependencies, deterministic critical-path worship, resource-infeasible parallelism, stale published plans, churn from over-reactive replanning, and schedule padding. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Optimal schedules are often fragile to duration and availability error; schedule stability and implementability can dominate nominal makespan. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Baseline schedules evolved into reactive, predictive–reactive, rolling-horizon and online scheduling policies. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | The schedule is a current decision policy with explicit recomputation and freeze/stability rules, not an archival chart. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Daily replanning rituals are optional; material state-triggered currentness is the property. |

### P034 — Use work-conserving execution only within conflict, option, safety, and congestion bounds
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | HYBRID_RESOLUTION |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Scheduling theory, queueing service disciplines, online algorithms and capacity/option-value reasoning. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Do not idle a machine when eligible work is waiting, under objectives where non-idling is optimal or admissible. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | ‘Always keep resources busy’ is generalised beyond the assumptions that justify non-idling. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Starting work consumes scarce WIP/acceptance capacity, blocks higher-value arrivals, creates setup costs, destroys options or increases risk. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Starting work consumes scarce WIP/acceptance capacity, blocks higher-value arrivals, creates setup costs, destroys options or increases risk. |
| MECHANISM | Define eligible work and conflict bounds; compare marginal start value with queue, setup, option, safety and switching consequences; allow intentional idle time when justified. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Ready work exists but starting it could create shared-resource conflict, WIP, lock-in, setup, safety or priority harm. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Start the highest-value conflict-free work; remain idle when no eligible work has positive net consequence. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A schedule owner must be able to allocate constrained resources, resolve conflicts, change priorities, and re-plan after state changes. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Completion time, tardiness, service, risk, stability, switching/setup cost, resource feasibility, and acceptance constraints are distinguished. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Precedence, release dates, resource/skill needs, setup and blocking conditions, duration uncertainty, deadlines, current progress, and shared validation capacity. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Precedence and resource constraints are real; task durations, preemption, parallelism, calendars, and availability are not treated as certain unless justified. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Breakdowns, rework, duration error, arrivals, resource loss, and changing priorities are represented through buffers, policies, scenarios, or rolling rescheduling as warranted. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Machines, people, skills, processors, test/acceptance channels, external approvals, and switching costs are explicit. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Fewer resource conflicts, less avoidable blocking, earlier completion of genuinely independent work, and controlled adaptation to changed state. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The operational coordinator and resource owners who can execute and revise the schedule. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Confusing shared project labels with dependencies, deterministic critical-path worship, resource-infeasible parallelism, stale published plans, churn from over-reactive replanning, and schedule padding. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Optimal schedules are often fragile to duration and availability error; schedule stability and implementability can dominate nominal makespan. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Classical non-idling rules were narrowed by release/priority/setup/robustness/energy/switching and option-preservation contexts. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Execution is work-conserving relative to a truthful eligibility and consequence model, not relative to raw worker/machine availability. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A blanket non-idling rule is rejected; bounded productive dispatch is retained. |

### P035 — Value inventory, buffers, slack, and reserve conditionally rather than categorically
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | INVENTORY_AND_CAPACITY_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | QUEUEING_OR_INVENTORY_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | EOQ, stochastic inventory, safety stock, production-flow and real-option traditions. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Balance setup/order, holding, shortage and service costs; retain stock against uncertain demand. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | ‘Inventory is waste’ or ‘slack is safety’ is treated as a universal rule. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Too little buffer causes shortages, coupling and recovery failure; too much creates cost, obsolescence, delay and hidden WIP. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Too little buffer causes shortages, coupling and recovery failure; too much creates cost, obsolescence, delay and hidden WIP. |
| MECHANISM | Classify buffer purpose; model variability, lead/recovery time, service/shortage consequence, coupling, perishability and holding cost; place decoupling where it changes flow. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Variable demand or supply, long recovery/replenishment, coupled stages, service commitments, irreversible shortages or failure recovery. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use observed stockouts/backlogs, lead time and holding/shortage asymmetry to set a bounded rule; avoid formula transfer without fit. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The owner must control inventory, time reserve, WIP limits, capacity reserve, or staged commitment and be accountable for both shortage and holding costs. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Service, waiting, stockout, obsolescence, carrying cost, recovery, coupling, and option value are represented rather than treating all slack as waste or all buffer as safety. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Demand/arrival variability, lead times, replenishment/recovery time, perishability, shortage consequence, coupling, and cost of reserve. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Demand, replenishment, substitution, service-level, and cost structures fit the operating context sufficiently for quantitative sizing. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Demand, supply, duration, failure, and recovery uncertainty determine whether reserve has value. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Inventory, spare capacity, time, cash, attention, and recovery resources are treated as costly options. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Lower shortage and overload exposure, better decoupling, and preserved recovery or commitment options at an explicit cost. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of capacity, inventory, commitment timing, or recovery policy. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Universal zero-inventory or universal-safety-stock rules, buffers that hide defects, stale reserve levels, and reserve converted into a utilisation target. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Buffer value is context-specific; excessive reserve can increase cost, obsolescence, delay, moral hazard, and hidden WIP. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Deterministic lot size evolved into stochastic service-level, multi-echelon, robust, perishable and option-aware buffer decisions. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Every buffer has an owned purpose, cost, trigger, sizing basis and retirement/recalibration rule. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | EOQ, safety-stock formula or WIP board is optional; conditional buffer economics is the property. |

| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Demand/arrival variability, lead times, replenishment/recovery time, perishability, shortage consequence, coupling, and cost of reserve. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Demand, replenishment, substitution, service-level, and cost structures fit the operating context sufficiently for quantitative sizing. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Demand, supply, duration, failure, and recovery uncertainty determine whether reserve has value. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Inventory, spare capacity, time, cash, attention, and recovery resources are treated as costly options. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Lower shortage and overload exposure, better decoupling, and preserved recovery or commitment options at an explicit cost. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of capacity, inventory, commitment timing, or recovery policy. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Universal zero-inventory or universal-safety-stock rules, buffers that hide defects, stale reserve levels, and reserve converted into a utilisation target. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Buffer value is context-specific; excessive reserve can increase cost, obsolescence, delay, moral hazard, and hidden WIP. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Single-period critical fractile and fill-rate models expanded to service distributions, multi-echelon, robust and nonstationary policies. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Service level is a value/constraint decision with uncertainty and distributional consequences, not an optimisation package default. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A newsvendor formula is optional; owned overage–underage reasoning is the property. |

### P037 — Use mathematical optimisation only when decision complexity and value warrant it
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | MATHEMATICAL_PROGRAMMING_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | MATHEMATICAL_PROGRAMMING_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Linear/integer programming, assignment, network flow, scheduling and later computational optimisation. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Search a large constrained feasible set for a best objective value. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Optimisation is applied ceremonially to simple, dominated or already-discriminated decisions, or omitted where combinatorial/resource complexity has high consequence. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Either needless model/solver burden or avoidable resource loss from crude manual allocation. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Either needless model/solver burden or avoidable resource loss from crude manual allocation. |
| MECHANISM | Estimate decision stakes, feasible-space complexity, coupling, repeatability and achievable improvement; compare simple baselines and escalate to exact/approximate optimisation only when net value is positive. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Many interacting alternatives/constraints, scarce resources, repeated decisions, non-obvious trade-offs and material payoff. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Direct feasibility/dominance test, greedy/list heuristic or small enumeration with explicit regret bound where possible. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must approve the represented objective, constraints, alternatives, tolerances, and implementation rules; solver output is advice unless authority is explicitly automated. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The mathematical objective is traceable to valued consequences; hard constraints are enforceable; penalties, scaling, and proxies are challengeable. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Coefficients, feasible sets, capacities, costs, forecasts, and current state have provenance and uncertainty appropriate to their leverage on the solution. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Functional form, linearity/convexity, integrality, independence, horizon, decomposition, and numerical tolerances are stated and tested where material. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Sensitivity, out-of-sample performance, scenario or ambiguity analysis, and model-form uncertainty are addressed according to consequence. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Formulation, solve time, compute, data maintenance, implementation effort, and switching/reconfiguration costs are part of the decision. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Transparent resource trade-offs and high-value improvements in complex feasible spaces where simpler discrimination is inadequate. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of the allocation, design, policy, or schedule and the operators who must implement it. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Optimising the wrong objective, infeasible or unenforceable constraints, numerical false precision, brittle point estimates, local optimum/global harm, and solver optimality worship. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Formal optimality is conditional on the model; small optimality gaps can coexist with large real-world regret, and more exact algorithms do not repair misspecification. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Exact LP broadened to mixed-integer, nonlinear, decomposition, approximation, heuristics and rolling optimisation, while mature practice re-emphasises formulation and implementation. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Optimisation is a proportionate decision instrument with baseline comparison, validity evidence, sensitivity and implementability—not a badge. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | No solver, language or formulation is mandatory; resource-discriminating optimisation is the property only when warranted. |

| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Resources are spent proving negligible mathematical improvement, or a numerically acceptable solution violates a consequential real constraint. |
| MECHANISM | Translate gaps/tolerances into decision units and consequence bounds; compare with data/model uncertainty and implementation granularity; tighten only where action or feasibility can change. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Large/exact optimisation, close alternatives, numerically sensitive constraints, binary thresholds or costly solve time. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Check whether the incumbent and bound imply different real actions; stop if not and model uncertainty dominates. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must approve the represented objective, constraints, alternatives, tolerances, and implementation rules; solver output is advice unless authority is explicitly automated. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The mathematical objective is traceable to valued consequences; hard constraints are enforceable; penalties, scaling, and proxies are challengeable. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Coefficients, feasible sets, capacities, costs, forecasts, and current state have provenance and uncertainty appropriate to their leverage on the solution. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Functional form, linearity/convexity, integrality, independence, horizon, decomposition, and numerical tolerances are stated and tested where material. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Sensitivity, out-of-sample performance, scenario or ambiguity analysis, and model-form uncertainty are addressed according to consequence. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Formulation, solve time, compute, data maintenance, implementation effort, and switching/reconfiguration costs are part of the decision. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Transparent resource trade-offs and high-value improvements in complex feasible spaces where simpler discrimination is inadequate. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of the allocation, design, policy, or schedule and the operators who must implement it. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Optimising the wrong objective, infeasible or unenforceable constraints, numerical false precision, brittle point estimates, local optimum/global harm, and solver optimality worship. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Formal optimality is conditional on the model; small optimality gaps can coexist with large real-world regret, and more exact algorithms do not repair misspecification. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Algorithmic convergence criteria were supplemented by application-specific tolerances, approximation quality and decision-relative stopping. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Numerical precision is subordinate to consequence and model uncertainty; report both mathematical and real-decision uncertainty. |

### P041 — Distinguish variability, parameter uncertainty, ambiguity, model-form error, and nonstationarity
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | STATISTICAL_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Bayesian/Savage decision theory, Ellsberg ambiguity, stochastic/robust optimisation and simulation uncertainty analysis. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Represent known probability distributions or subjective probabilities for uncertain states. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | All uncertainty is collapsed into one distribution, confidence interval or scenario list. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | A method robust to sampled variability is claimed robust to misspecified models, structural breaks or unknown state spaces. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | A method robust to sampled variability is claimed robust to misspecified models, structural breaks or unknown state spaces. |
| MECHANISM | Classify uncertainty source and epistemic status; select sensitivity, stochastic, robust, distributionally robust, scenario, adaptive or abstention mechanisms accordingly. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Material uncertain demand, duration, cost, state transition, model class, preference or external regime. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use separate labels and bounds; avoid assigning probabilities where identification is weak. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |

| ORIGINAL_FORM | Choose first-stage action, observe uncertainty, then take feasible recourse at a cost. |

| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | The model overstates downside by ignoring feasible correction or understates it by assuming unavailable recourse. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | The model overstates downside by ignoring feasible correction or understates it by assuming unavailable recourse. |

| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Decisions that remain acceptable across credible states and can adapt or recover when the realised state differs from the nominal forecast. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner who bears downside and can fund hedges, reserves, recourse, or staged commitment. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Invented distributions, narrow scenarios, blanket worst-case conservatism, ambiguity sets tuned after the fact, infeasible recourse, and robustness to parameters but not model class. |

| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Set-inclusive worst case evolved into tractable ellipsoidal/polyhedral, budgeted, adjustable and data-driven distributional robustness. |

### P045 — Use scenarios and stress tests without claiming future-event completeness
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONVERGENT_PROPERTY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Stochastic programming scenarios, risk-informed decision making, robust optimisation and simulation practice. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Evaluate decisions over representative uncertain states or sampled scenarios. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A finite scenario set is treated as exhaustive or selected to support a preferred decision. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Unrepresented correlation, regime change or model-form failure defeats the recommendation while ‘scenario coverage’ creates false confidence. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Unrepresented correlation, regime change or model-form failure defeats the recommendation while ‘scenario coverage’ creates false confidence. |
| MECHANISM | Document generation and exclusion logic, include correlated/adversarial stress states, test sensitivity to scenario set/weights, and preserve residual uncertainty. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Uncertain high-consequence decisions where analytic distributions are weak or several interacting disruptions matter. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use a small transparent set: nominal, plausible adverse, tail/common-cause and recovery-failure cases. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must define acceptable downside, risk, confidence, robustness, recourse, and the cost of conservatism. |

| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Decisions that remain acceptable across credible states and can adapt or recover when the realised state differs from the nominal forecast. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner who bears downside and can fund hedges, reserves, recourse, or staged commitment. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Invented distributions, narrow scenarios, blanket worst-case conservatism, ambiguity sets tuned after the fact, infeasible recourse, and robustness to parameters but not model class. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Robust, stochastic, chance-constrained, and distributionally robust methods protect against different uncertainty statements; none is universally mature without fit and calibration evidence. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Fixed planning scenarios expanded into scenario optimisation, stress testing, ambiguity sets, exploratory modelling and adaptive monitoring. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Scenarios challenge decisions and expose breakpoints; they do not certify that the future has been enumerated. |

### P046 — Carry forecast uncertainty and decision loss into operational choices
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | DATA_DRIVEN_OPTIMISATION_TRANSLATION |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | STATISTICAL_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Probabilistic forecasting, proper scoring rules, stochastic inventory/capacity models and forecast-combination research. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Estimate demand or state, then insert a point forecast or distribution into an operational model. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Forecast accuracy is evaluated separately from the asymmetric, constrained and state-dependent loss of the downstream decision. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | A lower-error forecast yields higher shortage, congestion, inventory, service or intervention cost; optimisation treats an estimate as known truth. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | A lower-error forecast yields higher shortage, congestion, inventory, service or intervention cost; optimisation treats an estimate as known truth. |
| MECHANISM | Use calibrated probabilistic forecasts or explicit error scenarios; propagate uncertainty into the decision; evaluate by out-of-sample decision consequence as well as predictive score; test bias, structural break and feedback. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Forecast-controlled inventory, capacity, staffing, scheduling, maintenance, admission, pricing or resource allocation where error changes action. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use a conservative interval, break-even error bound, or simple high/low demand discriminator when a full predictive distribution cannot alter the chosen action. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must define acceptable downside, risk, confidence, robustness, recourse, and the cost of conservatism. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Expected performance, tail consequence, regret, reliability, service, recourse cost, and opportunity cost are distinguished. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Probability estimates, scenarios, intervals, ambiguity sets, correlations, tail evidence, and recourse costs have provenance and calibration limits. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Known probabilities, uncertainty-set coverage, distributional family, stage structure, observability, recourse feasibility, and stationarity are explicit. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Aleatory variability, parameter uncertainty, model-form uncertainty, ambiguity, nonstationarity, and unknown unknowns are not conflated. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Reserve, hedging, recourse capacity, sensing, reconfiguration, and opportunity cost are represented. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Decisions that remain acceptable across credible states and can adapt or recover when the realised state differs from the nominal forecast. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner who bears downside and can fund hedges, reserves, recourse, or staged commitment. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Invented distributions, narrow scenarios, blanket worst-case conservatism, ambiguity sets tuned after the fact, infeasible recourse, and robustness to parameters but not model class. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Robust, stochastic, chance-constrained, and distributionally robust methods protect against different uncertainty statements; none is universally mature without fit and calibration evidence. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Point forecast plus deterministic optimisation evolved toward probabilistic forecasts, forecast combinations, stochastic/robust decisions, judgment-aware forecasting and decision-focused learning. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Prediction quality and decision quality are both measured; uncertainty, intervention feedback and regime sensitivity remain visible through implementation. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A sophisticated forecast model is not the property; decision-relevant calibration and consequence propagation are. |

### P047 — Use state-contingent policies and rolling re-optimisation for revisable decisions
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | SEQUENTIAL_OR_ONLINE_DECISION_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONTROL_THEORY_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Dynamic programming, Markov decision processes, receding/rolling-horizon planning, online optimisation and dynamic scheduling. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Choose a policy mapping observed state to action rather than a single open-loop action sequence. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A published one-shot plan remains authoritative after demand, capacity, task completion, failures or information have changed. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Stale allocations and schedules accumulate infeasibility, delay or cost while nominal adherence is mistaken for control. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Stale allocations and schedules accumulate infeasibility, delay or cost while nominal adherence is mistaken for control. |
| MECHANISM | Define observable state, review/replan events, horizon, frozen commitments, switching costs, recourse and authority; re-estimate and re-optimise only when changed state can alter action materially. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Sequential work with material state revelation, uncertain durations/demand, failures, arrivals, or recoverable commitments. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use simple event-triggered rules or a short rolling priority list when exact dynamic optimisation is unnecessary. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The policy owner must control observations, update cadence, action authority, exploration limits, and switching or lock-in costs. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Immediate reward/cost, future state, learning value, safety/constraint violation, switching cost, and long-horizon consequences are represented. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | State observations, transition/feedback data, delay, censoring, intervention effects, and nonstationarity are measured or bounded. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | State sufficiency, transition structure, feedback timing, horizon/discounting, exploration safety, and policy class are explicit. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Unknown dynamics, delayed feedback, drift, partial observability, and exploration risk are treated as first-class burdens. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Sensing, computation, experimentation capacity, reconfiguration effort, and operational slack constrain adaptation. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | State-contingent action, controlled learning, and timely re-optimisation without pretending that a static plan predicts the future. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The operator or automated controller with explicit authority and guardrails. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | One-shot plans in changing systems, oscillatory replanning, reward misspecification, unsafe exploration, delayed-feedback bias, and lock-in ignored by rolling optimisation. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Formal regret or policy guarantees are environment- and model-dependent; reinforcement learning is one translation, not the universal endpoint. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Bellman recursion and MDPs broadened into rolling-horizon scheduling, model-predictive and online optimisation, learning-augmented policies and human override. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | The operational object is a governed update policy with state/currentness evidence—not a frozen schedule pretending to predict the future. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Continuous re-solving is not required; state-linked reconsideration and bounded commitment are the property. |

### P050 — Verify implementation and validate simulation against its decision purpose
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_VALIDITY_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | SIMULATION_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | OPERATIONS_RESEARCH_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Discrete-event/Monte Carlo simulation methodology, model verification and validation, and engineering model-governance practice. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Check that the simulation is correctly implemented and adequately represents the real system for its intended use. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Detailed animation, calibration or plausible output is mistaken for decision-valid representation. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | A simulation faithfully executes the wrong logic, fits history for the wrong reasons, or is reused outside its validated domain. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | A simulation faithfully executes the wrong logic, fits history for the wrong reasons, or is reused outside its validated domain. |
| MECHANISM | Separate conceptual-model validity, code verification, data/input validity, operational/face comparison, sensitivity, predictive/decision validation and documented use domain; involve independent challenge where consequence warrants. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Simulation output materially changes design, capacity, schedule, policy, safety margin, investment or resource allocation. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | For low-consequence questions, use hand checks, extreme cases and comparison with observed/simple analytical behaviour. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A decision owner must specify the decision question, acceptance criteria, and how simulation evidence will alter action. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The model estimates decision-relevant consequences and uncertainty rather than maximising detail, animation realism, or run count. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Input distributions, correlations, initial conditions, warm-up, random streams, calibration data, and output measures are controlled and documented. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Conceptual model, boundary, causal structure, stochastic inputs, stationarity, and extrapolation regime are explicit. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Monte Carlo error, input uncertainty, parameter uncertainty, model-form uncertainty, rare-event coverage, and scenario uncertainty are separated. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Run budget, model-building effort, validation evidence, data acquisition, and analyst attention are finite. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Safer experimentation with complex stochastic systems and quantified consequence ranges when analytic or live experimentation is impractical. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The decision owner and domain experts who can challenge model structure and interpret output. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Many replications of a wrong model, animation-as-validation, dependence between replications, unhandled transients, calibration to history mistaken for intervention validity, and simulation optimum worship. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Verification can show correct implementation of the conceptual model, not truth of the conceptual model; validation is purpose- and domain-relative. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Verification/validation checklists matured toward iterative credibility assessment, input/model-form uncertainty and decision-context governance rather than universal ‘validation’ claims. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | A simulation has a bounded credibility claim tied to a decision, state, data regime and consequence—not a certificate that the model is true. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | An elaborate V&V dossier is proportional to consequence; challengeable credibility evidence is the property. |

### P051 — Control replications, transients, dependence, and input uncertainty in simulation evidence
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_VALIDITY_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | SIMULATION_LINEAGE |

| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Monte Carlo output analysis, regenerative/steady-state simulation, input modelling and variance/uncertainty analysis. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Use independent random replications, appropriate warm-up/run length and statistical output analysis. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | More runs reduce Monte Carlo noise but leave initialisation bias, dependence, input estimation and model-form uncertainty untouched. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Narrow confidence intervals around the wrong or biased model create false precision, especially for rare events and nonstationary systems. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Narrow confidence intervals around the wrong or biased model create false precision, especially for rare events and nonstationary systems. |
| MECHANISM | Define estimand and horizon; control random streams; diagnose warm-up/transients/autocorrelation; quantify input uncertainty; use variance reduction/rare-event methods when justified; report model-form uncertainty separately. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Stochastic simulation comparisons whose differences are near decision thresholds or whose tail/steady-state claims matter. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use common random numbers plus a few independent replications and a consequence-based precision target; stop when ranking is stable enough for the decision. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A decision owner must specify the decision question, acceptance criteria, and how simulation evidence will alter action. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The model estimates decision-relevant consequences and uncertainty rather than maximising detail, animation realism, or run count. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Input distributions, correlations, initial conditions, warm-up, random streams, calibration data, and output measures are controlled and documented. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Conceptual model, boundary, causal structure, stochastic inputs, stationarity, and extrapolation regime are explicit. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Monte Carlo error, input uncertainty, parameter uncertainty, model-form uncertainty, rare-event coverage, and scenario uncertainty are separated. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Run budget, model-building effort, validation evidence, data acquisition, and analyst attention are finite. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Safer experimentation with complex stochastic systems and quantified consequence ranges when analytic or live experimentation is impractical. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The decision owner and domain experts who can challenge model structure and interpret output. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Many replications of a wrong model, animation-as-validation, dependence between replications, unhandled transients, calibration to history mistaken for intervention validity, and simulation optimum worship. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Verification can show correct implementation of the conceptual model, not truth of the conceptual model; validation is purpose- and domain-relative. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Run-count rules evolved toward designed experiments, sequential stopping, input-uncertainty intervals, metamodels and integrated simulation optimisation. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Replication budget is tied to decision precision; independent statistical error, input uncertainty and structural uncertainty are not conflated. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Thousands of runs are not inherently credible; error-controlled evidence at decision-relevant precision is. |

### P052 — Test multi-criteria rankings against weights, scales, normalisation, thresholds, and method choice
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | MULTI_CRITERIA_DECISION_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | DECISION_ANALYSIS_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | MAUT/AHP/outranking and multi-objective decision analysis; rank-reversal and robustness criticism. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Aggregate criterion performance using elicited weights, utility/value functions or pairwise comparison. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A numerical rank is presented as objective despite unstable preferences, incompatible scales, alternative-dependent normalisation or compensatory assumptions. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Small, politically convenient or post-hoc changes to weights, bounds, criteria or alternatives reverse the winner while the matrix hides that fragility. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Small, politically convenient or post-hoc changes to weights, bounds, criteria or alternatives reverse the winner while the matrix hides that fragility. |
| MECHANISM | Validate scale type and independence assumptions; expose normalisation; run weight/score/method sensitivity, rank acceptability and dominance/non-compensatory checks; preserve ties or undecided sets where warranted. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Trade studies or MCDA where criteria conflict and the top alternatives are close or preference inputs are contested. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use dominance, threshold and break-even-weight analysis; omit scoring when a hard constraint or clear dominance settles the choice. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | A legitimate decision owner and affected stakeholders must own criteria, thresholds, weights, vetoes, and aggregation rules. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Criteria meanings, scale type, non-compensatory limits, stakeholder conflicts, and uncertainty are explicit; a total score is not presumed to be value truth. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Alternative performance evidence, scale definitions, normalisation rules, weights or preference statements, and uncertainty ranges are traceable. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Preferential/utility independence, cardinality, compensability, commensurability, and aggregation-method assumptions are explicit. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Weight, score, threshold, normalisation, and alternative-set sensitivity are analysed where they could change ranking or admissibility. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Elicitation, facilitation, dispute resolution, data collection, and sensitivity analysis costs are proportionate to consequence. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Transparent, challengeable trade-offs and preservation of Pareto, veto, and stakeholder information that a single proxy would erase. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The accountable owner and stakeholders whose values are represented or whose disagreement is preserved. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Rank reversal, arbitrary normalisation, false cardinal arithmetic on ordinal scores, compensating across hard limits, post-hoc weights, and spreadsheet objectivity theatre. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Different MCDA methods embody different value models and can rank the same alternatives differently; explicit judgement is not eliminated by arithmetic. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Fixed weighted sums broadened toward MAUT, outranking, Pareto methods, stochastic/robust MCDA and sensitivity/acceptability analysis. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | The output is a conditional preference map and robustness statement, not a discovered objective ranking. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A scored matrix is optional; explicit, challengeable value trade-offs and sensitivity are the property. |

| FIELD_OR_OPERATIONAL_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH | LOW |
| IMPLEMENTATION_CASE_STRENGTH | HIGH |
| REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH | MODERATE |
| TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH | HIGH |

### P053 — Detect and resist objective, constraint, data, queue, and reporting gaming
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | STRONGLY_RETAINED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONVERGENT_PROPERTY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Goodhart/Campbell effects, principal-agent and performance-measurement criticism, algorithmic fairness and model-governance research. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Set operational targets and monitor performance against them. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Once control, reward or legitimacy depends on a metric/model, actors can reclassify work, shift costs, change weights, omit constraints or select scenarios to manufacture success. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | The optimisation surface improves while real consequence worsens; post-hoc model revision makes a preferred alternative appear optimal. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | The optimisation surface improves while real consequence worsens; post-hoc model revision makes a preferred alternative appear optimal. |
| MECHANISM | Maintain decision-frame and model-change provenance; use independent outcome measures, anti-gaming audits, frozen-before-result assumptions where warranted, distributional checks and explicit classification of legitimate revision versus evaluator capture. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | High-stakes KPIs, allocation rules, service levels, ranked alternatives, algorithmic control, incentives or politically contested optimisation. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use a direct outcome plus one counter-metric and inspect boundary cases/reclassifications; avoid composite scores where direct authority suffices. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The owner of the real consequence must be distinct from owners rewarded on the proxy, with authority to audit and revise measures. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Proxy, target, constraint, distributional impact, externalities, and opportunities for reclassification or cost shifting are explicit. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Metric provenance, denominators, missingness, threshold behaviour, classification changes, and outcome measures independent of the target are monitored. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | The proxy remains causally and institutionally linked to the valued outcome after it becomes a target. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Strategic adaptation and feedback-induced distribution shift are expected rather than treated as noise. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Independent outcome measurement, audit capacity, metric rotation or retirement, and exception review are funded. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Lower probability that optimisation improves the dashboard while degrading the system or shifting harm outside the model boundary. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The consequence owner, affected stakeholders, and governance authority—not only the metric-producing unit. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Threshold gaming, queue hiding, backlog reclassification, schedule padding, cost shifting, dropped constraints, selective scenarios, and post-hoc weights. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Anti-gaming controls themselves can create complexity and new gaming surfaces; the mature form prefers direct consequences and plural indicators where feasible. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Metric criticism expanded into causal/performance monitoring, fairness/externality constraints, performative prediction and governed model revision. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Targets are treated as interventions in a socio-technical system, with protected provenance and independent consequences that can invalidate the metric. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | More dashboards are not anti-gaming; independent consequence evidence and change control are. |

### P054 — Validate data-driven and decision-focused models in the deployed decision loop
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | DATA_DRIVEN_OPTIMISATION_TRANSLATION |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | DOMAIN_TRANSLATION |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Predict-then-optimise, decision-focused learning, performative prediction and recent AI–OR integration. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Train predictors or end-to-end models to improve downstream optimisation loss rather than prediction accuracy alone. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Historical empirical risk or differentiable surrogate performance is treated as proof of deployed decision improvement. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Endogenous/biased data, shift, selective labels, decision feedback, misspecified constraints or optimiser exploitation produce brittle or harmful recommendations out of sample. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Endogenous/biased data, shift, selective labels, decision feedback, misspecified constraints or optimiser exploitation produce brittle or harmful recommendations out of sample. |
| MECHANISM | Use held-out and prospective decision-consequence evaluation; test shift, feedback, calibration, constraint violations and counterfactual baselines; compare simple predict-then-optimise and heuristics; monitor after deployment with authority and rollback. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Learned predictions, costs, constraints, policies or surrogate solvers materially control operational decisions. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Prefer a transparent calibrated predictor plus robust/simple decision rule when end-to-end learning has no demonstrated incremental decision value. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The downstream decision owner must approve the loss, constraints, training regime, deployment policy, monitoring, and fallback authority. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Out-of-sample decision consequence, safety, fairness, robustness, compute and implementation cost—not prediction score alone—define value. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Training/deployment provenance, censoring, intervention feedback, leakage, shift, uncertainty, labels, and representativeness are assessed. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Training data support the deployment regime; the optimisation layer is differentiable/solvable as claimed; constraints and ambiguity sets remain meaningful. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Distribution shift, endogenous data, model error, uncertainty-set calibration, nonstationarity and feedback are first-class. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Training and solve cost, latency, monitoring, retraining, fallback, and human review are part of the engineering case. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Prediction and learning effort targeted at consequential errors, with explicit monitoring and fallback when the deployment regime changes. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The downstream decision owner, operators, and affected stakeholders. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Better prediction metrics but worse decisions, overfitting a decision layer, brittle constraints, hidden feedback, uncalibrated ambiguity sets, and benchmark-to-field transfer claims. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Decision-focused learning and RL can improve formal downstream loss under benchmark assumptions, but current external-validity, safety, scalability and implementation evidence remains uneven. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Separated prediction/optimisation expanded into decision-focused training, differentiable optimisation, performative feedback and learned ambiguity sets, while deployment validation burdens increased. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | A learned model is one component in a current, monitored decision system; the evidence claim is prospective consequence under the deployed loop, not benchmark loss alone. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | AI, differentiable solvers or end-to-end training are not evolved endpoints; demonstrated decision value under valid constraints is. |

| SCALING_OR_WEIGHTING_RISK | Weights, penalties or units can dominate results without reflecting consequence |
| VALIDATION | Trace objective and constraints to observed consequence, authority and implementability |
| CHEAP_PATH | Prefer a transparent calibrated predictor plus robust/simple decision rule when end-to-end learning has no demonstrated incremental decision value. |
| MATURE_FORM | A learned model is one component in a current, monitored decision system; the evidence claim is prospective consequence under the deployed loop, not benchmark loss alone. |

### P055 — Monitor realised consequences and retire or revise models after drift
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | STRONGLY_RETAINED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | CONVERGENT_PROPERTY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Operational OR implementation, rolling planning, forecast evaluation, model-risk governance and feedback-aware decision systems. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Compare implemented recommendations with operational outcomes and update when assumptions no longer hold. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A validated model, schedule, forecast, queue policy or metric becomes stale while its output continues to control action. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Drift, changed incentives, altered service processes or new constraints silently invalidate the decision logic; failure is blamed on execution without testing the model. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Drift, changed incentives, altered service processes or new constraints silently invalidate the decision logic; failure is blamed on execution without testing the model. |
| MECHANISM | Define outcome and leading indicators, assumption/currentness checks, override and incident channels, review cadence/event triggers, version ownership, rollback and retirement criteria; distinguish model, data and implementation defects. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Recurring or automated decisions, long-lived models, changing demand/capacity, adaptive adversaries, or high-consequence recommendations. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | For one-off reversible choices, record the outcome and a bounded reopen trigger; do not establish permanent monitoring machinery. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The operational authority, data owner, model owner, affected users, and override/escalation rights must be explicit. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The implementable consequence, not mathematical recommendation alone, is the success criterion. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Live data freshness, local constraints, exceptions, incentives, override behaviour, and post-decision outcomes are observable. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Operators can execute the recommendation, incentives do not systematically defeat it, and the model remains current after deployment. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Human adaptation, workarounds, changing incentives, trust calibration, and organisational drift are treated as model uncertainty. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Training, integration, change effort, exception handling, maintenance, and feedback capacity are included. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Recommendations that survive contact with authority, workflow, incentives, data latency, and operator knowledge. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The people or automated systems that act, plus the authority that owns exceptions and consequences. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Technically superior but unusable recommendations, shadow systems, stale models, selective compliance, unowned overrides, and blaming users for revealed model defects. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Adoption is not proof of validity and resistance is not proof of irrationality; implementation can reveal missing constraints or conflicting objectives. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | One-time implementation studies expanded into model lifecycle governance, online evaluation, drift monitoring, performative-feedback analysis and explicit retirement. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Validity is time-bounded and consequence-tested; a model remains authoritative only while owned evidence supports its current decision use. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A monitoring dashboard is optional; currentness evidence, outcome feedback and retirement authority are the property. |

### P056 — Preserve near-optimal alternatives and portfolios when model discrimination is weak
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | HYBRID_RESOLUTION |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Multiple optima in mathematical programming, Pareto sets, sensitivity analysis, robust optimisation and analysis-of-alternatives practice. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Report the optimiser's selected optimum, alternative optima, or an efficient frontier. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | A tiny modelled objective difference is converted into a categorical organisational commitment despite uncertainty and unmodelled implementation attributes. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | The nominal winner is fragile, hard to implement or dominated after small parameter changes, while acceptable options and flexibility are discarded. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | The nominal winner is fragile, hard to implement or dominated after small parameter changes, while acceptable options and flexibility are discarded. |
| MECHANISM | Generate epsilon/near-optimal sets, efficient portfolios or materially indistinguishable alternatives; compare implementation, robustness, option value and stakeholder consequences; retain choice until evidence discriminates. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Close objective values, substantial parameter/weight uncertainty, several feasible implementations, or high switching/irreversibility cost. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Report ties and break-even ranges rather than force a single rank; keep two feasible options alive when cheap. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The decision owner must approve the represented objective, constraints, alternatives, tolerances, and implementation rules; solver output is advice unless authority is explicitly automated. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The mathematical objective is traceable to valued consequences; hard constraints are enforceable; penalties, scaling, and proxies are challengeable. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Coefficients, feasible sets, capacities, costs, forecasts, and current state have provenance and uncertainty appropriate to their leverage on the solution. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Functional form, linearity/convexity, integrality, independence, horizon, decomposition, and numerical tolerances are stated and tested where material. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Sensitivity, out-of-sample performance, scenario or ambiguity analysis, and model-form uncertainty are addressed according to consequence. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Formulation, solve time, compute, data maintenance, implementation effort, and switching/reconfiguration costs are part of the decision. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Transparent resource trade-offs and high-value improvements in complex feasible spaces where simpler discrimination is inadequate. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The owner of the allocation, design, policy, or schedule and the operators who must implement it. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Optimising the wrong objective, infeasible or unenforceable constraints, numerical false precision, brittle point estimates, local optimum/global harm, and solver optimality worship. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Formal optimality is conditional on the model; small optimality gaps can coexist with large real-world regret, and more exact algorithms do not repair misspecification. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Single-solution optimisation broadened toward Pareto fronts, sensitivity regions, robust/near-optimal sets, scenario portfolios and human selection among transparent options. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Optimisation narrows and structures the choice set; it does not manufacture certainty beyond model resolution. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Enumerating every near-optimum is unnecessary; preserving materially indistinguishable choices and flexibility is the property. |

### P057 — A named solver or optimisation algorithm is not a universal engineering property
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | MATHEMATICAL_PROGRAMMING_LINEAGE |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | MATHEMATICAL_PROGRAMMING_NATIVE |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | The proliferation of simplex, branch-and-bound, decomposition, convex, dynamic, heuristic and metaheuristic solver families. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Select an algorithm suited to a represented mathematical structure and computational budget. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Solver use or algorithmic sophistication is treated as evidence that the underlying decision has been engineered. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | A wrong objective, missing alternative, invalid distribution or infeasible implementation is solved faster or more exactly without improving the real decision. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | A wrong objective, missing alternative, invalid distribution or infeasible implementation is solved faster or more exactly without improving the real decision. |
| MECHANISM | Treat algorithms as conditional implementations chosen after framing, formulation, assumption and value-of-computation tests; compare simple rules and preserve solver-independent validation. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Only when a formal model has a live decision consumer and computational complexity materially prevents useful discrimination. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Enumeration, dominance, a direct constraint, rule, greedy heuristic or manual calculation when it settles the decision reliably. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | No artefact or named method acquires authority merely by being produced; an accountable decision owner remains required. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The underlying decision consequence must be recovered from the ritualised proxy or artefact. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Evidence must address whether the artefact changes decisions or operations, not merely whether it exists or is detailed. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Method-specific assumptions are not silently universalised. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Uncertainty hidden by deterministic artefacts, precise scores, or repeated computation is surfaced. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Ceremony cost and opportunity cost are counted. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Lower bureaucracy and retention of the transferable mechanism without mandatory branding or artefact form. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | Only a live decision or operational consumer can justify the practice. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Tool worship, compliance-only production, false precision, and replacing model validity with algorithm or artefact completion. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | The named practice may still be useful in a bounded context; rejection applies to its elevation into a universal property. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Algorithm families became more powerful and specialised, but mature practice increasingly separates computational optimality from model and implementation validity. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | No solver family is admitted as a general property; the surviving property is fit-for-decision computation under verified formulation and bounded cost. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Solver branding, certificates and dashboards are artefacts; they are not independent evidence of decision quality. |

### P060 — One-hundred-percent utilisation as an efficiency target is rejected
| Field | Frozen disposition |

| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Simplified production/accounting utilisation targets contrasted with queueing and heavy-traffic theory. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Keep expensive resources continuously busy to avoid apparent idle cost. |

| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Near saturation causes explosive waiting, abandonment, backlog, missed deadlines and no room for surge or maintenance; local busy-ness degrades system throughput. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Near saturation causes explosive waiting, abandonment, backlog, missed deadlines and no room for surge or maintenance; local busy-ness degrades system throughput. |
| MECHANISM | Reject maximal utilisation as a universal target; choose load/reserve by variability, service consequence, bottleneck, recovery and cost; monitor queue and tail delay as well as throughput. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Variable-demand service or production systems with finite waiting consequence and uncertain capacity. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Maintain a simple load threshold and reserve band based on observed delay/backlog; do not require a parametric queue model when data invalidate one. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | No artefact or named method acquires authority merely by being produced; an accountable decision owner remains required. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The underlying decision consequence must be recovered from the ritualised proxy or artefact. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Evidence must address whether the artefact changes decisions or operations, not merely whether it exists or is detailed. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Method-specific assumptions are not silently universalised. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Uncertainty hidden by deterministic artefacts, precise scores, or repeated computation is surfaced. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Ceremony cost and opportunity cost are counted. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Lower bureaucracy and retention of the transferable mechanism without mandatory branding or artefact form. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | Only a live decision or operational consumer can justify the practice. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Tool worship, compliance-only production, false precision, and replacing model validity with algorithm or artefact completion. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | The named practice may still be useful in a bounded context; rejection applies to its elevation into a universal property. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Queueing theory, heavy-traffic analysis and service operations established the utilisation–delay trade-off; modern systems use admission control, autoscaling and surge reserve. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Idle capacity can be an option and congestion-control resource; its value is consequence- and variability-dependent. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | A universal 70%, 80% or other target is also rejected; justified capacity policy is the property. |

### P063 — Metaheuristics are conditional search techniques, not universal engineering properties

### P064 — A giant integrated model is useful only when integration value exceeds opacity and maintenance cost
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_BUREAUCRATISED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | HYBRID |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | SYSTEMS_ANALYSIS_IMPORT_OR_SHARED_ANCESTRY |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Large-scale mathematical programming, military systems analysis, enterprise planning and integrated simulation/optimisation. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Represent many coupled decisions and constraints in one model to avoid inconsistent local optimisation. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Integration is pursued as completeness, creating an opaque, brittle model with no owner, slow updates and unchallengeable assumptions. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | The model becomes stale before use, hides domain-specific uncertainty, centralises illegitimate authority, or produces output no operator can implement or diagnose. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | The model becomes stale before use, hides domain-specific uncertainty, centralises illegitimate authority, or produces output no operator can implement or diagnose. |
| MECHANISM | Integrate only decision-coupled variables; use modular interfaces, decomposition, local validation, provenance and ownership; test whether a smaller model or coordination prices/rules provides the same discrimination. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Strong cross-system coupling where local decisions materially externalise cost and a shared model can be maintained and governed. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Coordinate a few binding interfaces, budgets or bottlenecks between smaller models rather than build an all-encompassing digital representation. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The operational authority, data owner, model owner, affected users, and override/escalation rights must be explicit. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The implementable consequence, not mathematical recommendation alone, is the success criterion. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Live data freshness, local constraints, exceptions, incentives, override behaviour, and post-decision outcomes are observable. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Operators can execute the recommendation, incentives do not systematically defeat it, and the model remains current after deployment. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Human adaptation, workarounds, changing incentives, trust calibration, and organisational drift are treated as model uncertainty. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Training, integration, change effort, exception handling, maintenance, and feedback capacity are included. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Recommendations that survive contact with authority, workflow, incentives, data latency, and operator knowledge. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The people or automated systems that act, plus the authority that owns exceptions and consequences. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Technically superior but unusable recommendations, shadow systems, stale models, selective compliance, unowned overrides, and blaming users for revealed model defects. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Adoption is not proof of validity and resistance is not proof of irrationality; implementation can reveal missing constraints or conflicting objectives. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Monolithic planning models were supplemented by decomposition, hierarchical/bi-level optimisation, modular simulation and problem-structuring approaches. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Integration scope is itself a value-of-information/maintenance decision; modularity is preferred unless coupling evidence warrants central representation. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Model size and data volume are not completeness; maintained decision-relevant coupling is the property. |

### P065 — Universal transfer of parametric queue, inventory, and scheduling formulas to knowledge or agent work remains unresolved
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | UNRESOLVED |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | ONLY_ANALOGOUS |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | UNRESOLVED_TENSION |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Classical queueing, inventory and scheduling models and their later metaphorical application to software, knowledge work and AI-agent systems. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Map arrivals, service times, servers, buffers, precedence and costs to a new operational domain and apply established formulas or algorithms. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Transferable congestion/dependency logic is conflated with validity of specific stationarity, independence, homogeneity, service-discipline and cost assumptions. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | A neat M/M/1, EOQ or machine-scheduling analogy ignores strategic task selection, learning, retries, shared acceptance, endogenous service, quality variation or changing task definitions. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | A neat M/M/1, EOQ or machine-scheduling analogy ignores strategic task selection, learning, retries, shared acceptance, endogenous service, quality variation or changing task definitions. |
| MECHANISM | Separate qualitative invariants—finite capacity, variability, WIP, bottlenecks, dependency, recourse—from parametric claims; empirically test arrivals, service, routing, feedback and consequence before quantitative transfer. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Novel service, software, knowledge or agentic systems where queue/capacity/schedule effects are plausible but the stochastic process is not established. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use direct WIP/backlog, elapsed-time, bottleneck and conflict observations; avoid distributional formulas until diagnostics support them. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | No artefact or named method acquires authority merely by being produced; an accountable decision owner remains required. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | The underlying decision consequence must be recovered from the ritualised proxy or artefact. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | Evidence must address whether the artefact changes decisions or operations, not merely whether it exists or is detailed. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | Method-specific assumptions are not silently universalised. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Uncertainty hidden by deterministic artefacts, precise scores, or repeated computation is surfaced. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Ceremony cost and opportunity cost are counted. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | Lower bureaucracy and retention of the transferable mechanism without mandatory branding or artefact form. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | Only a live decision or operational consumer can justify the practice. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | Tool worship, compliance-only production, false precision, and replacing model validity with algorithm or artefact completion. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | The named practice may still be useful in a bounded context; rejection applies to its elevation into a universal property. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Classical formulas expanded into networks, time-varying/heavy-tailed queues, learning-augmented algorithms and domain-specific empirical models; general transfer evidence remains incomplete. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Congestion and constraint reasoning are retained; exact formula transfer remains conditional and must be validated domain by domain. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Renaming tasks ‘jobs’ and workers ‘servers’ does not establish a queueing model. |
