### P066 — Use maintenance and replacement policies only with a credible failure-state and renewal model
| Field | Frozen disposition |
| --- | --- |
| CURRENT_STATUS | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC |
| LINEAGE_CLASS | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC |
| RELATIONSHIP_CLASS | INDUSTRIAL_ENGINEERING_HYBRID |
| HISTORICAL_ORIGIN | Renewal theory, age/block replacement, reliability economics and modern condition-based maintenance optimisation. |
| ORIGINAL_FORM | Choose preventive replacement or repair timing by balancing failure, downtime, inspection, maintenance and replacement costs under a life/failure distribution. |
| PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED | Calendar maintenance, run-to-failure, or predictive-maintenance output is treated as universally efficient without establishing deterioration, failure consequence, observability or repair effectiveness. |
| DECISION_OR_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_MODE | Premature replacement wastes capacity and parts; delayed intervention causes avoidable failure; sensor/prognostic error or common-cause dependence invalidates a nominal threshold policy. |
| FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT | Premature replacement wastes capacity and parts; delayed intervention causes avoidable failure; sensor/prognostic error or common-cause dependence invalidates a nominal threshold policy. |
| MECHANISM | Define failure states and consequence, deterioration/renewal assumptions, imperfect repair, inspection and observation quality, maintenance resource windows, spare capacity and recourse; compare corrective, preventive and condition-based policies out of sample. |
| TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT | Assets or services with material failure consequence, repeated life cycles, observable condition or age dependence, and controllable maintenance/replacement action. |
| NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH | Use manufacturer/field failure evidence, a conservative inspection interval, direct condition threshold or run-to-failure where consequence is low and replacement is cheap; avoid predictive optimisation without incremental value. |
| DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS | A live decision, a consequence-bearing consumer, and enough boundary information to distinguish alternatives. |
| DECISION_OWNER_OR_AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS | The policy owner must control observations, update cadence, action authority, exploration limits, and switching or lock-in costs. |
| OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_PRECONDITIONS | Immediate reward/cost, future state, learning value, safety/constraint violation, switching cost, and long-horizon consequences are represented. |
| DATA_OR_MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS | State observations, transition/feedback data, delay, censoring, intervention effects, and nonstationarity are measured or bounded. |
| MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS | State sufficiency, transition structure, feedback timing, horizon/discounting, exploration safety, and policy class are explicit. |
| UNCERTAINTY_PRECONDITIONS | Unknown dynamics, delayed feedback, drift, partial observability, and exploration risk are treated as first-class burdens. |
| RESOURCE_OR_CAPACITY_PRECONDITIONS | Sensing, computation, experimentation capacity, reconfiguration effort, and operational slack constrain adaptation. |
| EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF | State-contingent action, controlled learning, and timely re-optimisation without pretending that a static plan predicts the future. |
| DECISION_OR_CONSUMER | The operator or automated controller with explicit authority and guardrails. |
| KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES | One-shot plans in changing systems, oscillatory replanning, reward misspecification, unsafe exploration, delayed-feedback bias, and lock-in ignored by rolling optimisation. |
| IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS | Formal regret or policy guarantees are environment- and model-dependent; reinforcement learning is one translation, not the universal endpoint. |
| HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED | Age and block replacement models expanded into imperfect repair, multi-component and condition-based policies, joint operations-maintenance scheduling, prognostics and partially observed sequential control. |
| MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM | Maintenance is a state-contingent reliability-and-capacity decision whose policy is validated against actual failure behaviour, observation quality, downtime and resource coupling. |
| CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY | Predictive-maintenance branding, sensor volume or a fixed preventive calendar is not the property; consequence-grounded intervention timing is. |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_DECISION_FRAME_MODEL
A legitimate model begins downstream of a live decision frame. The minimum frame is an owner–action–deadline tuple, a non-impoverished alternative set, valued consequences, feasible/enforceable constraints, material uncertainty, implementation authority and a statement of what further evidence could change.

**Operational rules**

- Separate the real consequence from the tractable mathematical representation.
- Generate alternatives before ranking; record why status quo, deferment, pilot or rollback are absent when excluded.
- Distinguish hard constraints, soft preferences and implementation conditions.
- Treat elicited values and probabilities as owned inputs subject to sensitivity, not discovered facts.
- Escalate modelling effort only when the decision is consequential and unresolved by a cheaper discriminator.
- End with a choice, deferment, information action, policy or explicit non-decision owned by an authority.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** A completed trade study, model or review does not establish decision quality when the owner, consequence, feasible alternatives or authority is missing.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P001 — Explicit decision owner, consumer, deadline, and action authority | Any consequential allocation, schedule, optimisation, trade study, forecast-controlled action, or automated policy. | For low-consequence reversible choices, name one accountable chooser and a decision time; no formal charter is required. | Analysis begins with an owner-action-deadline tuple and ends in an implementable choice, deferment, experiment, policy, or documented non-decision. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S005, S006, S040, S073, S075, S076] |
| P002 — Frame the real decision and consequence before selecting a model | Whenever analysis will rank alternatives, allocate scarce resources, or automate action. | A one-page decision frame or direct authoritative constraint can suffice where alternatives are few and consequence is clear. | Model choice is downstream of a challengeable decision frame and can be changed without changing the underlying consequence statement. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S006, S040, S047, S071, S072, S073, S075] |
| P003 — Generate and preserve meaningful alternatives before ranking or optimisation | High-consequence, irreversible, novel or underperforming decisions; decisions where all listed options score poorly. | For routine choices, screen a small known set and ask explicitly whether a materially different option exists. | The decision set is treated as an engineered object with provenance, feasibility screening, dominance checks and a reopen rule. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S047, S074, S076, S035] |
| P004 — Include status quo, no-action, deferment, and staged commitment where feasible | Irreversible, capital-intensive, uncertain, novel, or rapidly changing decisions. | For urgent or mandatory action, record why no-action/deferment is infeasible instead of modelling it. | The choice set includes feasible inaction and timing policies, with their risks and foregone benefits, without presuming delay is valuable. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S035, S036, S040, S075, S076] |
| P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences | Any optimisation, schedule, allocation or scored trade study with limits or prerequisites. | Use direct admissibility screening before scoring; a hard authoritative discriminator can end the comparison. | Constraint status is challengeable and linked to enforcement, uncertainty, recourse and violation consequence; infeasibility is diagnostic, not proof that reality is impossible. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S022, S073, S076, S062] |
| P006 — Trace objectives to consequences and resist proxy substitution | Whenever a KPI, score, forecast loss, utilisation, throughput, service level, or learned reward controls incentives or action. | Where a direct outcome or authoritative constraint is observable, use it instead of a composite proxy. | A proxy remains provisional evidence about a consequence, with independent outcome validation and an explicit gaming/feedback model. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S006, S070, S105, S106, S107, S108] |
| P007 — Preserve multiple objectives, Pareto structure, and non-compensatory limits | Decisions with genuinely conflicting consequences, stakeholder values, quality attributes or fairness/efficiency tensions. | Use a small consequence table and dominance check; do not aggregate when one alternative clearly dominates or a hard threshold decides. | Conflict remains visible; aggregation is an owned preference model, not objective truth, and alternative rankings are tested across plausible preferences. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S081, S082, S083, S109] |
| P008 — Represent stakeholders, distributional effects, fairness, and externalities | Resource allocation, prioritisation, service access, public decisions, automated decisions, or any optimisation with material third-party effects. | State who gains, who waits, who pays and who bears risk; use hard policy constraints when legitimacy is already settled. | Efficiency is one consequence among others, and fairness formulation is an explicit authority/value choice tested against operational effects. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S041, S075, S083, S105, S109, S110] |
| P009 — Account for reversibility, irreversibility, option value, and staged commitment | Capital commitments, architecture lock-in, contracts, irreversible external actions, long-lived capacity and uncertain technology choices. | Use qualitative option-preservation and reversibility screening for small or poorly quantified decisions. | Decision depth and commitment scale are proportional to irreversibility; reversible options can be exercised cheaply while irreversible choices preserve learning value. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S035, S036, S039, S075] |
| P010 — Represent decision horizon, dependencies, and sequential coupling | Linked decisions, replenishment, scheduling, capacity investment, maintenance, adaptive policies and any action with material carry-over effects. | Use an explicit two-step consequence/dependency check when full dynamic programming is disproportionate. | The unit of decision is a state-contingent policy or staged commitment when future coupling matters, not a falsely independent one-shot optimum. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S004, S011, S012, S013, S035] |
| P011 — Match model fidelity and analysis depth to decision consequence | Any choice of modelling depth, simulation detail, data collection, solver exactness or review breadth. | Use bounds, dominance, sensitivity or a simple discriminator before building a richer model. | Use the least-cost model that is adequate to discriminate the consequential decision, with a reopen rule when state or sensitivity changes. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S043, S048, S049, S050, S073, S075] |
| P012 — Give cheap authoritative discriminators and simple heuristics precedence when sufficient | Low-consequence, reversible, time-limited, repeated or structurally simple decisions, and preliminary screening of complex decisions. | This property is itself the cheap path: apply the least expensive valid discriminator with explicit limits. | Simple rules are preferred when validated for the context and monitored for drift; complexity is justified by incremental decision value, not prestige. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S017, S043, S048, S049, S050, S073] |
| P013 — Bound information, analysis, and computation by expected decision value | Proposed experiments, reviews, model runs, scenario expansion, forecast improvement, exact solves and additional data collection. | Use a qualitative decision-change matrix: can this evidence change admissibility, ranking, timing or confidence enough to matter? | Continue only when plausible marginal decision improvement exceeds acquisition, delay and opportunity cost; preserve uncertainty where formal inputs are not defensible. | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY | [S038, S039, S049, S050, S127] |
| P014 — Use explicit stop and reopen rules tied to possible action change | Any iterative analysis, model review, schedule, forecast, allocation policy or decision-support system. | A verbal rule can suffice: stop when the next evidence cannot change action enough; reopen when it can. | Closure is conditional and evidence-bound, not permanent; re-analysis is event-triggered rather than calendar ritual. | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY | [S048, S049, S063, S073, S075] |
| P015 — State model assumptions and validity domain as part of the decision claim | Any formal model, simulation, forecast, queue formula, scorecard, optimisation or learned policy. | List only assumptions capable of changing action; use a direct caveat and fallback when validation is infeasible. | Claims are scoped: optimal/valid under a stated representation and current evidence, with explicit transfer and drift limits. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S027, S028, S084, S088, S089] |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Close rankings, uncertain coefficients, high consequence, disputed preferences, unstable forecasts or model choice ambiguity. | Use one-way break-even and dominance tests before global or probabilistic sensitivity analysis. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P017 — Correct for optimiser's curse and validate out-of-sample decision performance | Many alternatives, noisy estimated values, flexible models, data-driven objectives, close options or repeated model tuning. | Apply a winner's-curse caution, confidence interval and simple baseline comparison before elaborate correction. | Recommendation evidence includes expected out-of-sample consequence and uncertainty, not only best fitted objective. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S070, S067, S068, S069, S127] |
| P018 — Separate solver or model optimality from real-decision validity | Any solver-backed, simulation-optimised or learned recommendation. | State ‘optimal under this model’ and independently challenge the model with domain/authority checks. | No recommendation controls action solely because an optimiser converged; each validity layer has evidence and ownership. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S006, S007, S070, S084, S088, S098] |
| P019 — Establish implementation feasibility, operational authority, and usable decision support | Any recommendation requiring organisational behaviour, software integration, recurring operator use, or automated enforcement. | For one-off simple decisions, verify authority, resource availability and direct executability with the responsible operator. | Implementation is part of model validity; resistance can be evidence of missing constraints rather than a defect in users. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S073, S075, S076, S099, S100, S101, S102, S104] |
| P020 — Retire or rebuild stale models, schedules, forecasts, and metrics without a live consumer | Recurring dashboards, schedules, forecasts, optimisation models, simulations and decision policies. | Use an explicit expiry/review date and owner; archive immediately when no live decision depends on it. | Analytical authority is conditional on current state, current decision and active ownership; stale artefacts fail closed or become historical evidence only. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S063, S073, S096, S097, S101, S102, S124] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE_AND_CONSTRAINT_MODEL
Objectives are provisional operational representations of consequences; constraints are claims about admissibility and enforcement. Mature practice exposes provenance, compensation rules, proxy gaps, stakeholder distribution and sensitivity rather than treating coefficients as neutral facts.

**Operational rules**

- Trace each optimised metric to a consequence and affected party.
- Classify each constraint as physical, resource, legal/policy, ethical, probabilistic, soft or modelling convenience.
- Use non-compensatory thresholds where no amount of performance elsewhere legitimises violation.
- Expose weight, scale, penalty and normalisation choices and freeze/provenance them when gaming is plausible.
- Validate outcomes independently after optimisation changes behaviour or data.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** A high objective value, large penalty or weighted total is not evidence that the real objective improved or a hard limit was respected.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences | Any optimisation, schedule, allocation or scored trade study with limits or prerequisites. | Use direct admissibility screening before scoring; a hard authoritative discriminator can end the comparison. | Constraint status is challengeable and linked to enforcement, uncertainty, recourse and violation consequence; infeasibility is diagnostic, not proof that reality is impossible. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S022, S073, S076, S062] |
| P006 — Trace objectives to consequences and resist proxy substitution | Whenever a KPI, score, forecast loss, utilisation, throughput, service level, or learned reward controls incentives or action. | Where a direct outcome or authoritative constraint is observable, use it instead of a composite proxy. | A proxy remains provisional evidence about a consequence, with independent outcome validation and an explicit gaming/feedback model. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S006, S070, S105, S106, S107, S108] |
| P007 — Preserve multiple objectives, Pareto structure, and non-compensatory limits | Decisions with genuinely conflicting consequences, stakeholder values, quality attributes or fairness/efficiency tensions. | Use a small consequence table and dominance check; do not aggregate when one alternative clearly dominates or a hard threshold decides. | Conflict remains visible; aggregation is an owned preference model, not objective truth, and alternative rankings are tested across plausible preferences. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S081, S082, S083, S109] |
| P008 — Represent stakeholders, distributional effects, fairness, and externalities | Resource allocation, prioritisation, service access, public decisions, automated decisions, or any optimisation with material third-party effects. | State who gains, who waits, who pays and who bears risk; use hard policy constraints when legitimacy is already settled. | Efficiency is one consequence among others, and fairness formulation is an explicit authority/value choice tested against operational effects. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S041, S075, S083, S105, S109, S110] |
| P015 — State model assumptions and validity domain as part of the decision claim | Any formal model, simulation, forecast, queue formula, scorecard, optimisation or learned policy. | List only assumptions capable of changing action; use a direct caveat and fallback when validation is infeasible. | Claims are scoped: optimal/valid under a stated representation and current evidence, with explicit transfer and drift limits. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S027, S028, S084, S088, S089] |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Close rankings, uncertain coefficients, high consequence, disputed preferences, unstable forecasts or model choice ambiguity. | Use one-way break-even and dominance tests before global or probabilistic sensitivity analysis. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P038 — Treat formulation, infeasibility, and implementability as diagnostics | Any infeasible, weakly feasible, highly constrained or surprising optimisation result. | Manually check the small set of binding/conflicting constraints and ask operators whether the represented action can be executed. | Infeasibility and feasibility are evidence about the model–world relation, not final conclusions about the world. | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S022, S062, S073] |
| P043 — Treat tail, rare, irreversible, and high-consequence outcomes explicitly | Irreversible loss, catastrophic failure, strict service/safety thresholds, extreme latency or correlated disruption. | Use consequence-based worst credible case or hard threshold when probabilities are not identifiable. | Tail protection is matched to consequence and evidence; probabilities and confidence levels are owned assumptions, not objective facts. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S022, S032, S045, S054, S075] |
| P052 — Test multi-criteria rankings against weights, scales, normalisation, thresholds, and method choice | Trade studies or MCDA where criteria conflict and the top alternatives are close or preference inputs are contested. | Use dominance, threshold and break-even-weight analysis; omit scoring when a hard constraint or clear dominance settles the choice. | The output is a conditional preference map and robustness statement, not a discovered objective ranking. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S078, S079, S080, S081, S082, S083] |
| P053 — Detect and resist objective, constraint, data, queue, and reporting gaming | High-stakes KPIs, allocation rules, service levels, ranked alternatives, algorithmic control, incentives or politically contested optimisation. | Use a direct outcome plus one counter-metric and inspect boundary cases/reclassifications; avoid composite scores where direct authority suffices. | Targets are treated as interventions in a socio-technical system, with protected provenance and independent consequences that can invalidate the metric. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S105, S106, S107, S108, S109, S110, S096, S097] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_ALTERNATIVE_GENERATION_MODEL
The decision set is itself engineered. Optimisation and scoring can only select represented alternatives, so mature practice separates option generation, feasibility screening and evaluation, and preserves staged or near-optimal choices when evidence cannot discriminate.

**Operational rules**

- Generate from values, failure modes, process/technology variants, local knowledge and scenarios.
- Include no action, delay, pilot, rollback, hybrid and staged commitment when feasible.
- Use dominance and hard-constraint screening before detailed scoring.
- Represent dependencies between present and future decisions and the option value of waiting or preserving alternatives.
- Reopen the set when all options underperform or new state invalidates feasibility.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** The best represented option is not necessarily the best attainable real option.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P003 — Generate and preserve meaningful alternatives before ranking or optimisation | High-consequence, irreversible, novel or underperforming decisions; decisions where all listed options score poorly. | For routine choices, screen a small known set and ask explicitly whether a materially different option exists. | The decision set is treated as an engineered object with provenance, feasibility screening, dominance checks and a reopen rule. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S047, S074, S076, S035] |
| P004 — Include status quo, no-action, deferment, and staged commitment where feasible | Irreversible, capital-intensive, uncertain, novel, or rapidly changing decisions. | For urgent or mandatory action, record why no-action/deferment is infeasible instead of modelling it. | The choice set includes feasible inaction and timing policies, with their risks and foregone benefits, without presuming delay is valuable. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S035, S036, S040, S075, S076] |
| P007 — Preserve multiple objectives, Pareto structure, and non-compensatory limits | Decisions with genuinely conflicting consequences, stakeholder values, quality attributes or fairness/efficiency tensions. | Use a small consequence table and dominance check; do not aggregate when one alternative clearly dominates or a hard threshold decides. | Conflict remains visible; aggregation is an owned preference model, not objective truth, and alternative rankings are tested across plausible preferences. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S081, S082, S083, S109] |
| P009 — Account for reversibility, irreversibility, option value, and staged commitment | Capital commitments, architecture lock-in, contracts, irreversible external actions, long-lived capacity and uncertain technology choices. | Use qualitative option-preservation and reversibility screening for small or poorly quantified decisions. | Decision depth and commitment scale are proportional to irreversibility; reversible options can be exercised cheaply while irreversible choices preserve learning value. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S035, S036, S039, S075] |
| P010 — Represent decision horizon, dependencies, and sequential coupling | Linked decisions, replenishment, scheduling, capacity investment, maintenance, adaptive policies and any action with material carry-over effects. | Use an explicit two-step consequence/dependency check when full dynamic programming is disproportionate. | The unit of decision is a state-contingent policy or staged commitment when future coupling matters, not a falsely independent one-shot optimum. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S004, S011, S012, S013, S035] |
| P056 — Preserve near-optimal alternatives and portfolios when model discrimination is weak | Close objective values, substantial parameter/weight uncertainty, several feasible implementations, or high switching/irreversibility cost. | Report ties and break-even ranges rather than force a single rank; keep two feasible options alive when cheap. | Optimisation narrows and structures the choice set; it does not manufacture certainty beyond model resolution. | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY | [S007, S025, S041, S073, S077, S082] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_QUEUE_CAPACITY_MODEL
Queueing is system behaviour created by finite capacity, variability, routing, priority and feedback. Mature capacity governance jointly observes arrival/demand, service, WIP, waiting/tail consequence, bottlenecks, reserve and regime currentness; it does not maximise utilisation.

**Operational rules**

- Represent demand/arrival and service/capacity processes at the time scale that drives decisions.
- Measure visible and hidden queues, age, retries, rework, blocking and abandonment.
- Treat utilisation with waiting, tail latency and overload risk; reserve is conditional capacity, not waste.
- Find the end-to-end bottleneck and shared acceptance resources before adding parallel workers.
- Distinguish steady state from transient, time-varying and overloaded regimes.
- Validate any parametric queue abstraction before transfer to heterogeneous knowledge or agent work.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** Average capacity exceeding average demand does not establish acceptable delay or stability.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P021 — Represent demand, arrivals, service, capacity, and variability before capacity claims | Shared service systems with stochastic demand, backlogs, latency/service commitments or capacity investment. | Measure arrivals, completions, backlog age, utilisation and peak-to-average behaviour before fitting a parametric queue. | Use the least-assumptive demand/capacity representation that discriminates overload, waiting and reserve decisions, with transient validation. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S001, S002, S014, S015, S016, S052, S056] |
| P022 — Govern utilisation jointly with waiting, congestion, and tail performance | Variable demand, finite deadlines, latency-sensitive service, failure/retry loops or expensive queues. | Plot utilisation, queue age and tail delay together; reduce load or add reserve when congestion inflects. | Efficiency is assessed at system throughput and service consequence, not maximum busy fraction; controlled idle capacity can be rational. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S016, S051, S053, S054, S057] |
| P023 — Make queues, WIP, backlogs, blocking, and ageing visible | Multi-stage services, workflows, compute pipelines, maintenance, support, review or acceptance bottlenecks. | Count current WIP/backlog by age and stage; apply flow conservation/Little's Law only after boundary and stability checks. | Waiting work is a first-class system state with explicit ownership, ageing and downstream consequence; dashboards cannot erase queues by classification. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S014, S015, S057] |
| P024 — Identify system bottlenecks and optimise end-to-end flow rather than local utilisation | Networks, pipelines, multi-stage workflows, shared tests/approvals, production/service systems and interdependent resource pools. | Compare arrival/completion rates and queue age by stage; test whether adding local capacity changes end-to-end flow. | Capacity action is justified by marginal end-to-end consequence and accounts for bottleneck migration after intervention. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S009, S014, S017, S057] |
| P025 — Size capacity reserve and slack from variability, consequence, recovery, and coupling | Consequential delay/shortage, variable or bursty demand, slow recovery, failure-prone capacity or tightly coupled stages. | Use peak/backlog/recovery observations and a bounded reserve rule before fitting a full queue/inventory model. | Reserve is a priced hedge and recovery option, not waste or virtue; it is conditional, observable and periodically recalibrated. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S002, S051, S053, S057, S058] |
| P026 — Make admission, priority, and service discipline explicit | Overload, heterogeneous consequences, deadlines, finite capacity, competing classes or safety/mission priorities. | Use a transparent priority/ageing rule with explicit exceptions; avoid queueing optimisation when consequences clearly order work. | Service discipline is an owned policy with starvation, gaming, fairness and overload tests, not an accidental queue order. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | [S017, S056, S112] |
| P027 — Distinguish transient, nonstationary, overloaded, and feedback-congested regimes | Bursty service, incidents, releases, diurnal demand, structural breaks, retry systems, fast growth or recurrent overload. | Plot time series of demand, capacity, backlog and recovery; reject steady-state inference when backlog trends or regimes shift. | Capacity governance is regime-aware and monitors whether model assumptions and stability conditions currently hold. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S052, S053, S054, S055] |
| P028 — Model queue networks, shared bottlenecks, retries, rework, and blocking when coupled | Pipelines, review/test chains, distributed services, multi-stage maintenance, workflows with rework or common dependencies. | Draw a flow/queue map and identify shared resources/retry loops before using network formulas or simulation. | Coupling is represented at enough fidelity to avoid local-capacity and naive-parallelism errors; exact product-form assumptions are not presumed. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S009, S014, S054, S055] |
| P060 — One-hundred-percent utilisation as an efficiency target is rejected | Variable-demand service or production systems with finite waiting consequence and uncertain capacity. | Maintain a simple load threshold and reserve band based on observed delay/backlog; do not require a parametric queue model when data invalidate one. | Idle capacity can be an option and congestion-control resource; its value is consequence- and variability-dependent. | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | [S001, S002, S003, S050, S051, S052, S053, S054, S055] |
| P065 — Universal transfer of parametric queue, inventory, and scheduling formulas to knowledge or agent work remains unresolved | Novel service, software, knowledge or agentic systems where queue/capacity/schedule effects are plausible but the stochastic process is not established. | Use direct WIP/backlog, elapsed-time, bottleneck and conflict observations; avoid distributional formulas until diagnostics support them. | Congestion and constraint reasoning are retained; exact formula transfer remains conditional and must be validated domain by domain. | UNRESOLVED | [S002, S003, S018, S019, S050, S051, S052, S055, S057, S113, S119] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_SCHEDULING_MODEL
A schedule is an executable, state-dependent allocation policy over real precedence, resource and acceptance conflicts. It must account for uncertain timing, release/setup/blocking, ceilings and switching cost, and be recomputed after material state change.

**Operational rules**

- Do not infer dependency from shared issue/project labels; prove precedence or conflict.
- Parallelise only when resource, acceptance, external and congestion boundaries permit.
- Treat resource ceilings as constraints, never as a target to keep every resource busy.
- Use current duration/risk ranges and expose release, setup, blocking, preemption and deadlines.
- Balance rolling replanning against schedule stability with event thresholds and frozen near-term commitments.
- Retain PERT/CPM only as a bounded representation of precedence/current criticality.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** Publishing a schedule does not make it current, feasible or predictive after state drift.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P029 — Schedule parallel work from real precedence, resource, and acceptance conflicts | Multiple ready work units with potential dependency or resource interaction. | Topological plus resource-conflict screening and a simple list/dispatch rule. | Parallelism is authorised by current conflict evidence and recomputed after state changes; neither issue-wide serialisation nor maximal concurrency is default. | SCHEDULING_PROPERTY | [S017, S018, S019, S061, S062, S064] |
| P030 — Treat resource ceilings as constraints, not utilisation targets | Owner-supplied limits on workers, compute, money, concurrent jobs, external calls or review capacity. | Enforce the ceiling and choose the highest-value feasible ready work; do not add filler work to hit a utilisation metric. | Ceilings constrain admissible actions while utilisation remains an observed trade-off with delay, reserve and switching cost. | SCHEDULING_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S061, S062, S064, S112] |
| P031 — Represent uncertain duration, release, setup, blocking, and deadline structure | Multi-stage work with uncertain time, scarce skills, external dependencies, changeovers or service deadlines. | Use three-point/range estimates and obvious setup/blocking checks without claiming PERT distributional precision. | Published times are conditional forecasts with uncertainty and conflict semantics, not commitments that reality must obey. | SCHEDULING_PROPERTY | [S018, S060, S063, S064, S065, S066] |
| P032 — Recompute schedules and allocations after material state change | Task completion/failure, new work, duration overrun, resource loss, priority/constraint change or observed demand regime shift. | Re-run a simple priority/resource-conflict rule on current state instead of rebuilding a full optimisation. | The schedule is a current decision policy with explicit recomputation and freeze/stability rules, not an archival chart. | SCHEDULING_PROPERTY | [S052, S053, S060, S063, S064, S112] |
| P033 — Balance schedule stability against adaptive replanning and switching costs | Recurring rescheduling with setup, context-switch, commitment or coordination costs. | Use a minimum-improvement threshold and protect near-term committed work unless safety or feasibility changes. | Replan only when expected improvement or risk reduction exceeds disruption cost, with exceptions for hard constraints. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | [S063, S064, S066, S112] |
| P034 — Use work-conserving execution only within conflict, option, safety, and congestion bounds | Ready work exists but starting it could create shared-resource conflict, WIP, lock-in, setup, safety or priority harm. | Start the highest-value conflict-free work; remain idle when no eligible work has positive net consequence. | Execution is work-conserving relative to a truthful eligibility and consequence model, not relative to raw worker/machine availability. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | [S017, S054, S057, S112] |
| P058 — A fixed deterministic PERT/CPM/Gantt network is superseded as general schedule authority | Project work with meaningful dependency structure; deterministic networks are acceptable only when durations/resources are sufficiently stable for the decision. | Use a dependency list and identify the current longest/most constraining chain; recompute after material completion or delay. | Precedence and schedule-critical constraints are retained; the fixed chart as future truth is rejected. | SUPERSEDED_BY_STRONGER_FORM | [S015, S016, S017, S058, S059, S060, S061, S062, S063] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_BUFFER_SLACK_OPTION_MODEL
Inventory, WIP, time slack, capacity reserve and preserved alternatives are costly options. Their value depends on demand and lead-time variability, coupling, failure/shortage consequence, recovery/recourse, perishability and opportunity cost.

**Operational rules**

- Separate cycle stock, safety stock, WIP, queue buffer, time reserve, surge capacity and option-preserving delay.
- Size reserve to consequence and uncertainty rather than a universal lean or resilience slogan.
- Count holding, obsolescence, information delay and hidden-defect costs alongside shortage and recovery.
- Protect reserve from conversion into a utilisation target.
- Re-estimate when lead times, demand, failure behaviour or recourse capacity change.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** “Inventory bad” and “slack good” are both rejected as general rules.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P009 — Account for reversibility, irreversibility, option value, and staged commitment | Capital commitments, architecture lock-in, contracts, irreversible external actions, long-lived capacity and uncertain technology choices. | Use qualitative option-preservation and reversibility screening for small or poorly quantified decisions. | Decision depth and commitment scale are proportional to irreversibility; reversible options can be exercised cheaply while irreversible choices preserve learning value. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S035, S036, S039, S075] |
| P025 — Size capacity reserve and slack from variability, consequence, recovery, and coupling | Consequential delay/shortage, variable or bursty demand, slow recovery, failure-prone capacity or tightly coupled stages. | Use peak/backlog/recovery observations and a bounded reserve rule before fitting a full queue/inventory model. | Reserve is a priced hedge and recovery option, not waste or virtue; it is conditional, observable and periodically recalibrated. | QUEUE_CAPACITY_PROPERTY | [S002, S051, S053, S057, S058] |
| P030 — Treat resource ceilings as constraints, not utilisation targets | Owner-supplied limits on workers, compute, money, concurrent jobs, external calls or review capacity. | Enforce the ceiling and choose the highest-value feasible ready work; do not add filler work to hit a utilisation metric. | Ceilings constrain admissible actions while utilisation remains an observed trade-off with delay, reserve and switching cost. | SCHEDULING_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S061, S062, S064, S112] |
| P035 — Value inventory, buffers, slack, and reserve conditionally rather than categorically | Variable demand or supply, long recovery/replenishment, coupled stages, service commitments, irreversible shortages or failure recovery. | Use observed stockouts/backlogs, lead time and holding/shortage asymmetry to set a bounded rule; avoid formula transfer without fit. | Every buffer has an owned purpose, cost, trigger, sizing basis and retirement/recalibration rule. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S003, S004, S034, S035, S058, S059] |
| P036 — Choose service-level, shortage, backorder, and holding trade-offs explicitly | Inventory, staffing or reserve choices with explicit service or shortage consequence. | Use a policy threshold from authoritative service requirement and observed variability; do not estimate a full cost curve when not identifiable. | Service level is a value/constraint decision with uncertainty and distributional consequences, not an optimisation package default. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | [S004, S034, S058, S059] |
| P042 — Represent recourse and state-contingent corrective action | Multi-stage commitments, recoverable failures, adaptive staffing/scheduling, inventory replenishment or uncertain implementation. | List credible fallback actions and recovery limits; use scenario-specific rules before full stochastic programming. | Robustness is achieved partly through credible recoverability, with recourse capacity and authority validated rather than assumed. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S004, S020, S021, S022, S026, S030, S031, S127] |
| P066 — Use maintenance and replacement policies only with a credible failure-state and renewal model | Assets or services with material failure consequence, repeated life cycles, observable condition or age dependence, and controllable maintenance/replacement action. | Use manufacturer/field failure evidence, a conservative inspection interval, direct condition threshold or run-to-failure where consequence is low and replacement is cheap; avoid predictive optimisation without incremental value. | Maintenance is a state-contingent reliability-and-capacity decision whose policy is validated against actual failure behaviour, observation quality, downtime and resource coupling. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | [S131, S132] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_OPTIMISATION_MODEL
Optimisation is warranted when a valid representation of alternatives, resources, consequences and constraints is too coupled or large for a cheaper discriminator. Its output remains conditional on formulation, data, uncertainty and implementation; numerical certificates are not real-world validity certificates.

**Operational rules**

- Use the simplest formulation and algorithm that changes the decision reliably.
- Treat infeasibility, multiple optima, binding constraints and numerical instability as diagnostic evidence.
- Interpret objective gaps, tolerances and duals through real consequence and validity range.
- Correct selection bias and test out-of-sample realised decision loss.
- Preserve near-optimal alternatives when model resolution is weaker than nominal differences.
- Prefer modular/decomposed models unless integrated coupling has demonstrated value.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** Solver optimality means only “optimal for this represented model at this numerical tolerance”.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences | Any optimisation, schedule, allocation or scored trade study with limits or prerequisites. | Use direct admissibility screening before scoring; a hard authoritative discriminator can end the comparison. | Constraint status is challengeable and linked to enforcement, uncertainty, recourse and violation consequence; infeasibility is diagnostic, not proof that reality is impossible. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S022, S073, S076, S062] |
| P015 — State model assumptions and validity domain as part of the decision claim | Any formal model, simulation, forecast, queue formula, scorecard, optimisation or learned policy. | List only assumptions capable of changing action; use a direct caveat and fallback when validation is infeasible. | Claims are scoped: optimal/valid under a stated representation and current evidence, with explicit transfer and drift limits. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S027, S028, S084, S088, S089] |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Close rankings, uncertain coefficients, high consequence, disputed preferences, unstable forecasts or model choice ambiguity. | Use one-way break-even and dominance tests before global or probabilistic sensitivity analysis. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P017 — Correct for optimiser's curse and validate out-of-sample decision performance | Many alternatives, noisy estimated values, flexible models, data-driven objectives, close options or repeated model tuning. | Apply a winner's-curse caution, confidence interval and simple baseline comparison before elaborate correction. | Recommendation evidence includes expected out-of-sample consequence and uncertainty, not only best fitted objective. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S070, S067, S068, S069, S127] |
| P018 — Separate solver or model optimality from real-decision validity | Any solver-backed, simulation-optimised or learned recommendation. | State ‘optimal under this model’ and independently challenge the model with domain/authority checks. | No recommendation controls action solely because an optimiser converged; each validity layer has evidence and ownership. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S006, S007, S070, S084, S088, S098] |
| P037 — Use mathematical optimisation only when decision complexity and value warrant it | Many interacting alternatives/constraints, scarce resources, repeated decisions, non-obvious trade-offs and material payoff. | Direct feasibility/dominance test, greedy/list heuristic or small enumeration with explicit regret bound where possible. | Optimisation is a proportionate decision instrument with baseline comparison, validity evidence, sensitivity and implementability—not a badge. | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY | [S007, S008, S009, S010, S017, S073] |
| P038 — Treat formulation, infeasibility, and implementability as diagnostics | Any infeasible, weakly feasible, highly constrained or surprising optimisation result. | Manually check the small set of binding/conflicting constraints and ask operators whether the represented action can be executed. | Infeasibility and feasibility are evidence about the model–world relation, not final conclusions about the world. | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S022, S062, S073] |
| P039 — Interpret solver tolerances and optimality gaps through real-world regret | Large/exact optimisation, close alternatives, numerically sensitive constraints, binary thresholds or costly solve time. | Check whether the incumbent and bound imply different real actions; stop if not and model uncertainty dominates. | Numerical precision is subordinate to consequence and model uncertainty; report both mathematical and real-decision uncertainty. | ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE | [S007, S010, S017, S048, S070] |
| P040 — Use dual values and shadow prices as model-relative marginal signals | Resource allocation models with meaningful and stable constraints where marginal analysis could guide capacity or prioritisation. | Inspect binding constraints and perform a small finite change scenario rather than treating an infinitesimal dual as truth. | Dual information is a sensitivity clue within the current model and range, not standalone evidence of real-world value. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | [S007, S020, S030, S112] |
| P056 — Preserve near-optimal alternatives and portfolios when model discrimination is weak | Close objective values, substantial parameter/weight uncertainty, several feasible implementations, or high switching/irreversibility cost. | Report ties and break-even ranges rather than force a single rank; keep two feasible options alive when cheap. | Optimisation narrows and structures the choice set; it does not manufacture certainty beyond model resolution. | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY | [S007, S025, S041, S073, S077, S082] |
| P057 — A named solver or optimisation algorithm is not a universal engineering property | Only when a formal model has a live decision consumer and computational complexity materially prevents useful discrimination. | Enumeration, dominance, a direct constraint, rule, greedy heuristic or manual calculation when it settles the decision reliably. | No solver family is admitted as a general property; the surviving property is fit-for-decision computation under verified formulation and bounded cost. | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S014, S017, S020, S030, S037, S071, S072] |
| P064 — A giant integrated model is useful only when integration value exceeds opacity and maintenance cost | Strong cross-system coupling where local decisions materially externalise cost and a shared model can be maintained and governed. | Coordinate a few binding interfaces, budgets or bottlenecks between smaller models rather than build an all-encompassing digital representation. | Integration scope is itself a value-of-information/maintenance decision; modularity is preferred unless coupling evidence warrants central representation. | USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_BUREAUCRATISED | [S005, S006, S020, S030, S098, S099, S101, S112] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_UNCERTAINTY_AND_RECOURSE_MODEL
Uncertainty is not one scalar. Mature practice distinguishes variability, estimated parameters, ambiguity, model form, correlation, structural break and nonstationarity; selects stochastic, robust, stress or adaptive mechanisms accordingly; and validates recourse capacity and authority.

**Operational rules**

- Assign probabilities only where a defensible basis exists; do not launder ambiguity into precision.
- State which uncertainties each robustness claim covers and which it does not.
- Model when information arrives and which recourse actions remain feasible, affordable and authorised.
- Separate expected performance from tails, hard consequence and irreversibility.
- Use scenarios to challenge and discriminate, never to claim future completeness.
- Calibrate uncertainty/ambiguity protection and report opportunity cost.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** Robust to a parameter interval is not robust to wrong structure, feedback or regime change.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P041 — Distinguish variability, parameter uncertainty, ambiguity, model-form error, and nonstationarity | Material uncertain demand, duration, cost, state transition, model class, preference or external regime. | Use separate labels and bounds; avoid assigning probabilities where identification is weak. | The uncertainty claim states what is known, estimated, bounded, disputed or unmodelled, and does not overgeneralise protection. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S042, S044, S027, S028, S029, S086, S087] |
| P042 — Represent recourse and state-contingent corrective action | Multi-stage commitments, recoverable failures, adaptive staffing/scheduling, inventory replenishment or uncertain implementation. | List credible fallback actions and recovery limits; use scenario-specific rules before full stochastic programming. | Robustness is achieved partly through credible recoverability, with recourse capacity and authority validated rather than assumed. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S004, S020, S021, S022, S026, S030, S031, S127] |
| P043 — Treat tail, rare, irreversible, and high-consequence outcomes explicitly | Irreversible loss, catastrophic failure, strict service/safety thresholds, extreme latency or correlated disruption. | Use consequence-based worst credible case or hard threshold when probabilities are not identifiable. | Tail protection is matched to consequence and evidence; probabilities and confidence levels are owned assumptions, not objective facts. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S022, S032, S045, S054, S075] |
| P044 — Calibrate robustness to credible ambiguity rather than blanket conservatism | Material parameter/distribution uncertainty with unacceptable nominal fragility and enough evidence to bound plausible variation. | Use break-even sensitivity and a small set of credible adverse scenarios before full robust optimisation. | Robustness is a calibrated decision choice with explicit price, coverage claim and model-misspecification boundary. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S023, S024, S025, S026, S027, S028, S029, S033, S120, S121] |
| P045 — Use scenarios and stress tests without claiming future-event completeness | Uncertain high-consequence decisions where analytic distributions are weak or several interacting disruptions matter. | Use a small transparent set: nominal, plausible adverse, tail/common-cause and recovery-failure cases. | Scenarios challenge decisions and expose breakpoints; they do not certify that the future has been enumerated. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S027, S028, S030, S031, S075, S089] |
| P046 — Carry forecast uncertainty and decision loss into operational choices | Forecast-controlled inventory, capacity, staffing, scheduling, maintenance, admission, pricing or resource allocation where error changes action. | Use a conservative interval, break-even error bound, or simple high/low demand discriminator when a full predictive distribution cannot alter the chosen action. | Prediction quality and decision quality are both measured; uncertainty, intervention feedback and regime sensitivity remain visible through implementation. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S091, S092, S093, S094, S095, S124, S128] |
| P066 — Use maintenance and replacement policies only with a credible failure-state and renewal model | Assets or services with material failure consequence, repeated life cycles, observable condition or age dependence, and controllable maintenance/replacement action. | Use manufacturer/field failure evidence, a conservative inspection interval, direct condition threshold or run-to-failure where consequence is low and replacement is cheap; avoid predictive optimisation without incremental value. | Maintenance is a state-contingent reliability-and-capacity decision whose policy is validated against actual failure behaviour, observation quality, downtime and resource coupling. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | [S131, S132] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_SEQUENTIAL_ADAPTIVE_MODEL
For revisable decisions, the engineering object is a policy: observed state, action, recourse, update trigger, frozen commitment, switching cost, delayed feedback and stop/reopen authority. Learning is justified only when future decision value exceeds current exposure and cost.

**Operational rules**

- Represent state observability and delayed/censored feedback, not merely a nominal Markov state.
- Use event-triggered or rolling updates when state change can materially alter action.
- Apply hysteresis/minimum holds when frequent switching destroys value.
- Bound exploration by safety, irreversibility, authority and expected future information value.
- Retire or roll back policies when realised consequences invalidate assumptions.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** RL or continuous re-optimisation is not inherently more adaptive than a well-governed simple event rule.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P010 — Represent decision horizon, dependencies, and sequential coupling | Linked decisions, replenishment, scheduling, capacity investment, maintenance, adaptive policies and any action with material carry-over effects. | Use an explicit two-step consequence/dependency check when full dynamic programming is disproportionate. | The unit of decision is a state-contingent policy or staged commitment when future coupling matters, not a falsely independent one-shot optimum. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S004, S011, S012, S013, S035] |
| P014 — Use explicit stop and reopen rules tied to possible action change | Any iterative analysis, model review, schedule, forecast, allocation policy or decision-support system. | A verbal rule can suffice: stop when the next evidence cannot change action enough; reopen when it can. | Closure is conditional and evidence-bound, not permanent; re-analysis is event-triggered rather than calendar ritual. | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY | [S048, S049, S063, S073, S075] |
| P042 — Represent recourse and state-contingent corrective action | Multi-stage commitments, recoverable failures, adaptive staffing/scheduling, inventory replenishment or uncertain implementation. | List credible fallback actions and recovery limits; use scenario-specific rules before full stochastic programming. | Robustness is achieved partly through credible recoverability, with recourse capacity and authority validated rather than assumed. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S004, S020, S021, S022, S026, S030, S031, S127] |
| P047 — Use state-contingent policies and rolling re-optimisation for revisable decisions | Sequential work with material state revelation, uncertain durations/demand, failures, arrivals, or recoverable commitments. | Use simple event-triggered rules or a short rolling priority list when exact dynamic optimisation is unnecessary. | The operational object is a governed update policy with state/currentness evidence—not a frozen schedule pretending to predict the future. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S011, S012, S013, S063, S112, S118, S119] |
| P048 — Trade learning and exploration against operating consequence and information value | Repeated decisions with material uncertainty, learnable response, future reuse and safe/reversible experimentation. | Use historical/offline evidence, a deterministic discriminator, or a small controlled pilot when full adaptive exploration is unnecessary or unsafe. | Exploration is an authorised information investment with explicit consequence, transfer horizon, guardrails and stop/reopen rule—not an assumed virtue. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | [S039, S049, S118, S119] |
| P049 — Represent delayed and partial feedback, switching cost, lock-in, and hysteresis | Dynamic allocation, staffing, routing, algorithmic decision support or policy control with delayed outcomes and costly change. | Use a cooldown/minimum-hold rule and explicit delayed review window before building a full state-space model. | Adaptation is responsive but not reflexive: updates account for what is observable, when it becomes informative, and what changing course costs. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S011, S013, S096, S097, S112] |
| P055 — Monitor realised consequences and retire or revise models after drift | Recurring or automated decisions, long-lived models, changing demand/capacity, adaptive adversaries, or high-consequence recommendations. | For one-off reversible choices, record the outcome and a bounded reopen trigger; do not establish permanent monitoring machinery. | Validity is time-bounded and consequence-tested; a model remains authoritative only while owned evidence supports its current decision use. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S063, S070, S093, S096, S097, S100, S101, S104, S124] |
| P062 — Reinforcement learning is a domain translation, not the evolved endpoint | Repeated high-dimensional sequential decisions where interaction data, safe learning and demonstrable policy advantage exist. | Use a rule, bandit, rolling optimiser, supervised forecast plus policy, or human-in-the-loop decision support when these settle the operational need. | RL may implement selected adaptive properties in a valid domain; it does not define evolved decision engineering. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | [S012, S013, S117, S118, S103] |
| P066 — Use maintenance and replacement policies only with a credible failure-state and renewal model | Assets or services with material failure consequence, repeated life cycles, observable condition or age dependence, and controllable maintenance/replacement action. | Use manufacturer/field failure evidence, a conservative inspection interval, direct condition threshold or run-to-failure where consequence is low and replacement is cheap; avoid predictive optimisation without incremental value. | Maintenance is a state-contingent reliability-and-capacity decision whose policy is validated against actual failure behaviour, observation quality, downtime and resource coupling. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | [S131, S132] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_DECISION_ANALYSIS_MODEL
Decision analysis supplies a normative structure for acts, uncertain states, consequences, preferences and information. Mature engineering uses that structure while preserving descriptive limits, elicitation instability, stakeholder conflict and authority boundaries.

**Operational rules**

- Use dominance and requisite modelling before elaborate utility assessment.
- Treat utility/risk preferences as decision-owner models, not population facts.
- Test probabilities, weights and framing changes for decision reversal.
- Use value of information to decide what to learn, not just what to choose.
- Preserve unresolved value conflict instead of hiding it in an aggregate score.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** Normative coherence does not establish that elicited human preferences are stable, descriptive or legitimately aggregable.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P001 — Explicit decision owner, consumer, deadline, and action authority | Any consequential allocation, schedule, optimisation, trade study, forecast-controlled action, or automated policy. | For low-consequence reversible choices, name one accountable chooser and a decision time; no formal charter is required. | Analysis begins with an owner-action-deadline tuple and ends in an implementable choice, deferment, experiment, policy, or documented non-decision. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S005, S006, S040, S073, S075, S076] |
| P002 — Frame the real decision and consequence before selecting a model | Whenever analysis will rank alternatives, allocate scarce resources, or automate action. | A one-page decision frame or direct authoritative constraint can suffice where alternatives are few and consequence is clear. | Model choice is downstream of a challengeable decision frame and can be changed without changing the underlying consequence statement. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S006, S040, S047, S071, S072, S073, S075] |
| P003 — Generate and preserve meaningful alternatives before ranking or optimisation | High-consequence, irreversible, novel or underperforming decisions; decisions where all listed options score poorly. | For routine choices, screen a small known set and ask explicitly whether a materially different option exists. | The decision set is treated as an engineered object with provenance, feasibility screening, dominance checks and a reopen rule. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S047, S074, S076, S035] |
| P004 — Include status quo, no-action, deferment, and staged commitment where feasible | Irreversible, capital-intensive, uncertain, novel, or rapidly changing decisions. | For urgent or mandatory action, record why no-action/deferment is infeasible instead of modelling it. | The choice set includes feasible inaction and timing policies, with their risks and foregone benefits, without presuming delay is valuable. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S035, S036, S040, S075, S076] |
| P006 — Trace objectives to consequences and resist proxy substitution | Whenever a KPI, score, forecast loss, utilisation, throughput, service level, or learned reward controls incentives or action. | Where a direct outcome or authoritative constraint is observable, use it instead of a composite proxy. | A proxy remains provisional evidence about a consequence, with independent outcome validation and an explicit gaming/feedback model. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S006, S070, S105, S106, S107, S108] |
| P007 — Preserve multiple objectives, Pareto structure, and non-compensatory limits | Decisions with genuinely conflicting consequences, stakeholder values, quality attributes or fairness/efficiency tensions. | Use a small consequence table and dominance check; do not aggregate when one alternative clearly dominates or a hard threshold decides. | Conflict remains visible; aggregation is an owned preference model, not objective truth, and alternative rankings are tested across plausible preferences. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S081, S082, S083, S109] |
| P009 — Account for reversibility, irreversibility, option value, and staged commitment | Capital commitments, architecture lock-in, contracts, irreversible external actions, long-lived capacity and uncertain technology choices. | Use qualitative option-preservation and reversibility screening for small or poorly quantified decisions. | Decision depth and commitment scale are proportional to irreversibility; reversible options can be exercised cheaply while irreversible choices preserve learning value. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S035, S036, S039, S075] |
| P013 — Bound information, analysis, and computation by expected decision value | Proposed experiments, reviews, model runs, scenario expansion, forecast improvement, exact solves and additional data collection. | Use a qualitative decision-change matrix: can this evidence change admissibility, ranking, timing or confidence enough to matter? | Continue only when plausible marginal decision improvement exceeds acquisition, delay and opportunity cost; preserve uncertainty where formal inputs are not defensible. | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY | [S038, S039, S049, S050, S127] |
| P014 — Use explicit stop and reopen rules tied to possible action change | Any iterative analysis, model review, schedule, forecast, allocation policy or decision-support system. | A verbal rule can suffice: stop when the next evidence cannot change action enough; reopen when it can. | Closure is conditional and evidence-bound, not permanent; re-analysis is event-triggered rather than calendar ritual. | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY | [S048, S049, S063, S073, S075] |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Close rankings, uncertain coefficients, high consequence, disputed preferences, unstable forecasts or model choice ambiguity. | Use one-way break-even and dominance tests before global or probabilistic sensitivity analysis. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P052 — Test multi-criteria rankings against weights, scales, normalisation, thresholds, and method choice | Trade studies or MCDA where criteria conflict and the top alternatives are close or preference inputs are contested. | Use dominance, threshold and break-even-weight analysis; omit scoring when a hard constraint or clear dominance settles the choice. | The output is a conditional preference map and robustness statement, not a discovered objective ranking. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S078, S079, S080, S081, S082, S083] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_AND_STOPPING_MODEL
Another observation, review, model refinement, simulation run or optimisation step is justified only by plausible marginal decision improvement relative to delay, compute, experiment, attention and opportunity cost. The cheap path is a qualitative decision-change test; formal VOI requires credible probability and consequence models.

**Operational rules**

- Name the pending action and the remaining uncertainty or computation.
- Explain how the result could change feasibility, ranking, timing or policy.
- Estimate consequence if changed and cost of acquiring the result before the deadline.
- Stop when plausible marginal improvement cannot justify cost or when a direct discriminator settles action.
- Reopen when state/evidence changes enough to alter action—not merely because a calendar review occurs.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** More analysis is not automatically prudent; stopping is an engineering decision, not fatigue or ritual.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P011 — Match model fidelity and analysis depth to decision consequence | Any choice of modelling depth, simulation detail, data collection, solver exactness or review breadth. | Use bounds, dominance, sensitivity or a simple discriminator before building a richer model. | Use the least-cost model that is adequate to discriminate the consequential decision, with a reopen rule when state or sensitivity changes. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S043, S048, S049, S050, S073, S075] |
| P012 — Give cheap authoritative discriminators and simple heuristics precedence when sufficient | Low-consequence, reversible, time-limited, repeated or structurally simple decisions, and preliminary screening of complex decisions. | This property is itself the cheap path: apply the least expensive valid discriminator with explicit limits. | Simple rules are preferred when validated for the context and monitored for drift; complexity is justified by incremental decision value, not prestige. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S017, S043, S048, S049, S050, S073] |
| P013 — Bound information, analysis, and computation by expected decision value | Proposed experiments, reviews, model runs, scenario expansion, forecast improvement, exact solves and additional data collection. | Use a qualitative decision-change matrix: can this evidence change admissibility, ranking, timing or confidence enough to matter? | Continue only when plausible marginal decision improvement exceeds acquisition, delay and opportunity cost; preserve uncertainty where formal inputs are not defensible. | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY | [S038, S039, S049, S050, S127] |
| P014 — Use explicit stop and reopen rules tied to possible action change | Any iterative analysis, model review, schedule, forecast, allocation policy or decision-support system. | A verbal rule can suffice: stop when the next evidence cannot change action enough; reopen when it can. | Closure is conditional and evidence-bound, not permanent; re-analysis is event-triggered rather than calendar ritual. | VALUE_OF_INFORMATION_PROPERTY | [S048, S049, S063, S073, S075] |
| P048 — Trade learning and exploration against operating consequence and information value | Repeated decisions with material uncertainty, learnable response, future reuse and safe/reversible experimentation. | Use historical/offline evidence, a deterministic discriminator, or a small controlled pilot when full adaptive exploration is unnecessary or unsafe. | Exploration is an authorised information investment with explicit consequence, transfer horizon, guardrails and stop/reopen rule—not an assumed virtue. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | [S039, S049, S118, S119] |
| P051 — Control replications, transients, dependence, and input uncertainty in simulation evidence | Stochastic simulation comparisons whose differences are near decision thresholds or whose tail/steady-state claims matter. | Use common random numbers plus a few independent replications and a consequence-based precision target; stop when ranking is stable enough for the decision. | Replication budget is tied to decision precision; independent statistical error, input uncertainty and structural uncertainty are not conflated. | SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_VALIDITY_PROPERTY | [S085, S086, S087, S090, S111] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_MULTI_CRITERIA_MODEL
Multi-criteria methods make conflict and preference assumptions explicit; they do not discover an objective ranking. Mature practice uses dominance, thresholds, Pareto sets, requisite aggregation and sensitivity to weights, scores, scale, normalisation, method and stakeholder disagreement.

**Operational rules**

- Validate criterion meaning and scale before arithmetic.
- Distinguish compensatory trade-offs from veto, lexicographic and hard constraints.
- Expose whose preferences weights represent and whether utility independence is plausible.
- Test rank reversal and preserve ties/sets where inputs do not discriminate.
- Never post-hoc tune weights, alternatives or normalisation without provenance.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** A scored matrix is structured judgement, not objective measurement of preference truth.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences | Any optimisation, schedule, allocation or scored trade study with limits or prerequisites. | Use direct admissibility screening before scoring; a hard authoritative discriminator can end the comparison. | Constraint status is challengeable and linked to enforcement, uncertainty, recourse and violation consequence; infeasibility is diagnostic, not proof that reality is impossible. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S022, S073, S076, S062] |
| P007 — Preserve multiple objectives, Pareto structure, and non-compensatory limits | Decisions with genuinely conflicting consequences, stakeholder values, quality attributes or fairness/efficiency tensions. | Use a small consequence table and dominance check; do not aggregate when one alternative clearly dominates or a hard threshold decides. | Conflict remains visible; aggregation is an owned preference model, not objective truth, and alternative rankings are tested across plausible preferences. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S081, S082, S083, S109] |
| P008 — Represent stakeholders, distributional effects, fairness, and externalities | Resource allocation, prioritisation, service access, public decisions, automated decisions, or any optimisation with material third-party effects. | State who gains, who waits, who pays and who bears risk; use hard policy constraints when legitimacy is already settled. | Efficiency is one consequence among others, and fairness formulation is an explicit authority/value choice tested against operational effects. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S041, S075, S083, S105, S109, S110] |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Close rankings, uncertain coefficients, high consequence, disputed preferences, unstable forecasts or model choice ambiguity. | Use one-way break-even and dominance tests before global or probabilistic sensitivity analysis. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P052 — Test multi-criteria rankings against weights, scales, normalisation, thresholds, and method choice | Trade studies or MCDA where criteria conflict and the top alternatives are close or preference inputs are contested. | Use dominance, threshold and break-even-weight analysis; omit scoring when a hard constraint or clear dominance settles the choice. | The output is a conditional preference map and robustness statement, not a discovered objective ranking. | MULTI_CRITERIA_PROPERTY | [S041, S077, S078, S079, S080, S081, S082, S083] |
| P056 — Preserve near-optimal alternatives and portfolios when model discrimination is weak | Close objective values, substantial parameter/weight uncertainty, several feasible implementations, or high switching/irreversibility cost. | Report ties and break-even ranges rather than force a single rank; keep two feasible options alive when cheap. | Optimisation narrows and structures the choice set; it does not manufacture certainty beyond model resolution. | OPTIMISATION_PROPERTY | [S007, S025, S041, S073, S077, S082] |
| P059 — A universal weighted scorecard is rejected as an objective ranking mechanism | Only when cardinal value trade-offs are genuinely elicitable, compensatory aggregation is legitimate, and the result is robust enough for the decision. | Use hard-constraint screening, dominance, consequence tables and break-even weights; preserve explicit judgement where numbers add no discrimination. | Explicit challengeable trade-offs survive; a universal weighted scorecard does not. | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | [S041, S077, S078, S079, S080, S081, S082, S083] |
