## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_SIMULATION_VALIDITY_MODEL
Simulation earns decision authority through purpose-bounded verification, validation, input modelling, transient/output analysis, sensitivity and model-form challenge. Replication count addresses only one error source and is stopped at decision-relevant precision.

**Operational rules**

- Define the estimand, horizon, intervention and decision consequence first.
- Verify conceptual logic and code using traces, extreme cases and independent checks.
- Validate only for the intended decision/regime and preserve structural uncertainty.
- Control random streams, dependence, warm-up, run length and rare-event estimation.
- Allocate budget among replications, input learning and competing model forms by marginal decision value.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** A plausible animation, historical calibration or narrow confidence interval does not make a simulation true.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P011 — Match model fidelity and analysis depth to decision consequence | Any choice of modelling depth, simulation detail, data collection, solver exactness or review breadth. | Use bounds, dominance, sensitivity or a simple discriminator before building a richer model. | Use the least-cost model that is adequate to discriminate the consequential decision, with a reopen rule when state or sensitivity changes. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S043, S048, S049, S050, S073, S075] |
| P015 — State model assumptions and validity domain as part of the decision claim | Any formal model, simulation, forecast, queue formula, scorecard, optimisation or learned policy. | List only assumptions capable of changing action; use a direct caveat and fallback when validation is infeasible. | Claims are scoped: optimal/valid under a stated representation and current evidence, with explicit transfer and drift limits. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S027, S028, S084, S088, S089] |
| P050 — Verify implementation and validate simulation against its decision purpose | Simulation output materially changes design, capacity, schedule, policy, safety margin, investment or resource allocation. | For low-consequence questions, use hand checks, extreme cases and comparison with observed/simple analytical behaviour. | A simulation has a bounded credibility claim tied to a decision, state, data regime and consequence—not a certificate that the model is true. | SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_VALIDITY_PROPERTY | [S084, S088, S089, S090] |
| P051 — Control replications, transients, dependence, and input uncertainty in simulation evidence | Stochastic simulation comparisons whose differences are near decision thresholds or whose tail/steady-state claims matter. | Use common random numbers plus a few independent replications and a consequence-based precision target; stop when ranking is stable enough for the decision. | Replication budget is tied to decision precision; independent statistical error, input uncertainty and structural uncertainty are not conflated. | SIMULATION_OR_MODEL_VALIDITY_PROPERTY | [S085, S086, S087, S090, S111] |
| P061 — Simulation run count is not a general credibility property | Additional replications only when stochastic sampling error could change the decision relative to other uncertainty sources. | Use a small designed set of independent/common-random-number runs and consequence-based confidence bounds. | Runs buy only a bounded reduction in simulation sampling error; they do not validate the world model. | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | [S084, S085, S086, S087, S088, S089, S090, S111] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_FORECAST_TO_DECISION_MODEL
Forecasts are inputs to actions, not ends. Mature practice uses calibrated distributions or explicit error bounds, evaluates decision loss, propagates uncertainty, detects structural break and feedback, and compares end-to-end value with simple forecasts and policies.

**Operational rules**

- Use proper predictive evaluation and operational consequence evaluation together.
- Represent asymmetric decision loss and constraint violations, not average forecast error alone.
- Test combination, bias, leakage, shift and decision-induced data change.
- Monitor realised consequence and recalibrate or retire when the regime changes.
- Do not deploy decision-focused learning without a prospective decision-loop test and fallback.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** Lower RMSE or benchmark regret does not establish lower deployed operational cost.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Close rankings, uncertain coefficients, high consequence, disputed preferences, unstable forecasts or model choice ambiguity. | Use one-way break-even and dominance tests before global or probabilistic sensitivity analysis. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P017 — Correct for optimiser's curse and validate out-of-sample decision performance | Many alternatives, noisy estimated values, flexible models, data-driven objectives, close options or repeated model tuning. | Apply a winner's-curse caution, confidence interval and simple baseline comparison before elaborate correction. | Recommendation evidence includes expected out-of-sample consequence and uncertainty, not only best fitted objective. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S070, S067, S068, S069, S127] |
| P041 — Distinguish variability, parameter uncertainty, ambiguity, model-form error, and nonstationarity | Material uncertain demand, duration, cost, state transition, model class, preference or external regime. | Use separate labels and bounds; avoid assigning probabilities where identification is weak. | The uncertainty claim states what is known, estimated, bounded, disputed or unmodelled, and does not overgeneralise protection. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S042, S044, S027, S028, S029, S086, S087] |
| P046 — Carry forecast uncertainty and decision loss into operational choices | Forecast-controlled inventory, capacity, staffing, scheduling, maintenance, admission, pricing or resource allocation where error changes action. | Use a conservative interval, break-even error bound, or simple high/low demand discriminator when a full predictive distribution cannot alter the chosen action. | Prediction quality and decision quality are both measured; uncertainty, intervention feedback and regime sensitivity remain visible through implementation. | UNCERTAINTY_RECOURSE_PROPERTY | [S091, S092, S093, S094, S095, S124, S128] |
| P054 — Validate data-driven and decision-focused models in the deployed decision loop | Learned predictions, costs, constraints, policies or surrogate solvers materially control operational decisions. | Prefer a transparent calibrated predictor plus robust/simple decision rule when end-to-end learning has no demonstrated incremental decision value. | A learned model is one component in a current, monitored decision system; the evidence claim is prospective consequence under the deployed loop, not benchmark loss alone. | ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE | [S067, S068, S069, S096, S097, S120, S121, S103] |
| P055 — Monitor realised consequences and retire or revise models after drift | Recurring or automated decisions, long-lived models, changing demand/capacity, adaptive adversaries, or high-consequence recommendations. | For one-off reversible choices, record the outcome and a bounded reopen trigger; do not establish permanent monitoring machinery. | Validity is time-bounded and consequence-tested; a model remains authoritative only while owned evidence supports its current decision use. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S063, S070, S093, S096, S097, S100, S101, S104, S124] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_IMPLEMENTATION_AND_AUTHORITY_MODEL
A recommendation controls action legitimately only when feasible under actual resources and authority, legible enough to challenge, current enough for use, and connected to implementers, override, monitoring and retirement. Local adaptation may contain evidence rather than “resistance”.

**Operational rules**

- Identify owner, implementer, override and maintenance responsibility.
- Validate constraints against actual policy, skill, resource, latency and workflow.
- Expose recommendation stability and implementation/switching cost.
- Collect operator/local feedback and classify model, data, incentive and implementation defects separately.
- Retire models and dashboards with no live decision consumer.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** A mathematically superior recommendation that cannot be authorised, understood, executed or maintained is not an engineered decision.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P001 — Explicit decision owner, consumer, deadline, and action authority | Any consequential allocation, schedule, optimisation, trade study, forecast-controlled action, or automated policy. | For low-consequence reversible choices, name one accountable chooser and a decision time; no formal charter is required. | Analysis begins with an owner-action-deadline tuple and ends in an implementable choice, deferment, experiment, policy, or documented non-decision. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S005, S006, S040, S073, S075, S076] |
| P002 — Frame the real decision and consequence before selecting a model | Whenever analysis will rank alternatives, allocate scarce resources, or automate action. | A one-page decision frame or direct authoritative constraint can suffice where alternatives are few and consequence is clear. | Model choice is downstream of a challengeable decision frame and can be changed without changing the underlying consequence statement. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S006, S040, S047, S071, S072, S073, S075] |
| P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences | Any optimisation, schedule, allocation or scored trade study with limits or prerequisites. | Use direct admissibility screening before scoring; a hard authoritative discriminator can end the comparison. | Constraint status is challengeable and linked to enforcement, uncertainty, recourse and violation consequence; infeasibility is diagnostic, not proof that reality is impossible. | DECISION_FRAME_PROPERTY | [S007, S010, S022, S073, S076, S062] |
| P019 — Establish implementation feasibility, operational authority, and usable decision support | Any recommendation requiring organisational behaviour, software integration, recurring operator use, or automated enforcement. | For one-off simple decisions, verify authority, resource availability and direct executability with the responsible operator. | Implementation is part of model validity; resistance can be evidence of missing constraints rather than a defect in users. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S073, S075, S076, S099, S100, S101, S102, S104] |
| P020 — Retire or rebuild stale models, schedules, forecasts, and metrics without a live consumer | Recurring dashboards, schedules, forecasts, optimisation models, simulations and decision policies. | Use an explicit expiry/review date and owner; archive immediately when no live decision depends on it. | Analytical authority is conditional on current state, current decision and active ownership; stale artefacts fail closed or become historical evidence only. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S063, S073, S096, S097, S101, S102, S124] |
| P049 — Represent delayed and partial feedback, switching cost, lock-in, and hysteresis | Dynamic allocation, staffing, routing, algorithmic decision support or policy control with delayed outcomes and costly change. | Use a cooldown/minimum-hold rule and explicit delayed review window before building a full state-space model. | Adaptation is responsive but not reflexive: updates account for what is observable, when it becomes informative, and what changing course costs. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S011, S013, S096, S097, S112] |
| P053 — Detect and resist objective, constraint, data, queue, and reporting gaming | High-stakes KPIs, allocation rules, service levels, ranked alternatives, algorithmic control, incentives or politically contested optimisation. | Use a direct outcome plus one counter-metric and inspect boundary cases/reclassifications; avoid composite scores where direct authority suffices. | Targets are treated as interventions in a socio-technical system, with protected provenance and independent consequences that can invalidate the metric. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S105, S106, S107, S108, S109, S110, S096, S097] |
| P055 — Monitor realised consequences and retire or revise models after drift | Recurring or automated decisions, long-lived models, changing demand/capacity, adaptive adversaries, or high-consequence recommendations. | For one-off reversible choices, record the outcome and a bounded reopen trigger; do not establish permanent monitoring machinery. | Validity is time-bounded and consequence-tested; a model remains authoritative only while owned evidence supports its current decision use. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S063, S070, S093, S096, S097, S100, S101, S104, S124] |
| P064 — A giant integrated model is useful only when integration value exceeds opacity and maintenance cost | Strong cross-system coupling where local decisions materially externalise cost and a shared model can be maintained and governed. | Coordinate a few binding interfaces, budgets or bottlenecks between smaller models rather than build an all-encompassing digital representation. | Integration scope is itself a value-of-information/maintenance decision; modularity is preferred unless coupling evidence warrants central representation. | USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_BUREAUCRATISED | [S005, S006, S020, S030, S098, S099, S101, S112] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_PROXY_AND_OBJECTIVE_GAMING_MODEL
Optimised metrics change behaviour. Mature practice treats objectives, constraints, data and evaluation rules as an attack surface: provenance is preserved, independent consequences are monitored, model revisions are classified, and distributional/cost-shifting effects can invalidate apparent improvement.

**Operational rules**

- Trace KPI/objective to consequence and pair it with an independent outcome or counter-metric.
- Look for queue hiding, reclassification, threshold effects, selective scenarios and post-hoc weights.
- Freeze material assumptions before result where evaluator capture is plausible.
- Distinguish legitimate revision after new evidence from revision intended to make a favoured alternative win.
- Monitor feedback loops and affected groups after deployment.

**Anti-overclaim boundary:** Optimising a stable-looking proxy does not establish that the underlying target is stable or valid under intervention.

| Property | Trigger | Cheap path | Mature form | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P006 — Trace objectives to consequences and resist proxy substitution | Whenever a KPI, score, forecast loss, utilisation, throughput, service level, or learned reward controls incentives or action. | Where a direct outcome or authoritative constraint is observable, use it instead of a composite proxy. | A proxy remains provisional evidence about a consequence, with independent outcome validation and an explicit gaming/feedback model. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S006, S070, S105, S106, S107, S108] |
| P008 — Represent stakeholders, distributional effects, fairness, and externalities | Resource allocation, prioritisation, service access, public decisions, automated decisions, or any optimisation with material third-party effects. | State who gains, who waits, who pays and who bears risk; use hard policy constraints when legitimacy is already settled. | Efficiency is one consequence among others, and fairness formulation is an explicit authority/value choice tested against operational effects. | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | [S041, S075, S083, S105, S109, S110] |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Close rankings, uncertain coefficients, high consequence, disputed preferences, unstable forecasts or model choice ambiguity. | Use one-way break-even and dominance tests before global or probabilistic sensitivity analysis. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P053 — Detect and resist objective, constraint, data, queue, and reporting gaming | High-stakes KPIs, allocation rules, service levels, ranked alternatives, algorithmic control, incentives or politically contested optimisation. | Use a direct outcome plus one counter-metric and inspect boundary cases/reclassifications; avoid composite scores where direct authority suffices. | Targets are treated as interventions in a socio-technical system, with protected provenance and independent consequences that can invalidate the metric. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S105, S106, S107, S108, S109, S110, S096, S097] |
| P054 — Validate data-driven and decision-focused models in the deployed decision loop | Learned predictions, costs, constraints, policies or surrogate solvers materially control operational decisions. | Prefer a transparent calibrated predictor plus robust/simple decision rule when end-to-end learning has no demonstrated incremental decision value. | A learned model is one component in a current, monitored decision system; the evidence claim is prospective consequence under the deployed loop, not benchmark loss alone. | ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE | [S067, S068, S069, S096, S097, S120, S121, S103] |
| P055 — Monitor realised consequences and retire or revise models after drift | Recurring or automated decisions, long-lived models, changing demand/capacity, adaptive adversaries, or high-consequence recommendations. | For one-off reversible choices, record the outcome and a bounded reopen trigger; do not establish permanent monitoring machinery. | Validity is time-bounded and consequence-tested; a model remains authoritative only while owned evidence supports its current decision use. | STRONGLY_RETAINED | [S063, S070, S093, S096, S097, S100, S101, S104, S124] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_CEREMONY_STRIPPING_LEDGER
| PRACTICE_OR_ARTEFACT | UNDERLYING_PROPERTY | WHAT_IT_BUYS | WHEN_IT_FAILS | WHETHER_ARTEFACT_REQUIRED | ALTERNATIVE_IMPLEMENTATIONS | MODERN_DISPOSITION | PROPERTIES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Weighted trade matrix | Explicit alternatives, criteria, value judgements and sensitivity | Makes assumptions inspectable and can structure deliberation | Weights/scales/normalisation are unstable or post-hoc; hard constraints are made compensatory | NO | Dominance, consequence table, Pareto set, thresholds, deliberation | Conditional tool; universal objectivity claim rejected | [P007, P052, P059] |
| PERT/CPM/Gantt chart | Current precedence, resource and schedule-critical constraints | Communicates sequence and current timing hypothesis | Deterministic durations, missing resource conflicts, stale state and fixed critical path | NO | Dependency graph, rolling dispatch list, resource-constrained schedule, simulation | Underlying dependency property retained; fixed authority superseded | [P029, P032, P058] |
| Optimisation model | Explicit objective, alternatives, constraints and resource trade-offs | Can discriminate large coupled choice spaces and expose scarcity | Wrong objective/model solved exactly; no implementer; numerical optimum mistaken for reality | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | Enumeration, rule, heuristic, direct constraint, modular models | Trigger only when complexity and decision value warrant it | [P037, P038, P057] |
| Queueing formula | Demand/capacity/variability/congestion representation | Predicts delay, loss or reserve under fitted assumptions | Stationarity, independence or service definitions fail; transient overload or strategic work | NO | Direct backlog/age/load monitoring, simulation, empirical control limits | Qualitative queue properties transfer more broadly than parametric formula | [P021, P027, P065] |
| Monte Carlo simulation | Uncertainty propagation and counterfactual consequence | Handles complex stochastic systems not tractable analytically | Detailed but invalid model; input/model-form uncertainty ignored | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | Analytic bound, stress cases, historical replay, small experiment | Requires V&V and decision-linked precision | [P050, P051] |
| Thousands of simulation runs | Adequate stochastic precision for the decision | Reduces Monte Carlo sampling error | Other uncertainty dominates; runs are dependent or transient-biased | NO | Sequential confidence stopping, variance reduction, common random numbers | Run count itself rejected as credibility property | [P051, P061] |
| Resource-utilisation dashboard | Capacity, bottleneck, backlog and service consequence visibility | Can reveal load and reserve conditions | Maximal utilisation becomes target; hidden queues and tail delay ignored | NO | Backlog age, flow, tail latency, admission and reserve indicators | Utilisation is one conditional signal, never the objective alone | [P022, P023, P060] |
| Single “optimal” recommendation | Conditional discrimination among feasible alternatives | Can focus action where evidence is strong | Small model difference hides uncertainty or implementation differences | NO | Near-optimal set, Pareto frontier, break-even ranges, option portfolio | Retain alternatives when discrimination is weak | [P016, P017, P056] |
| Chance constraint with a precise confidence level | Explicit tolerated violation risk | Connects probabilistic uncertainty to feasibility | Probability model or confidence level lacks identification/authority | NO | Hard threshold, stress case, robust bound, contingency | Conditional on credible probability and consequence model | [P041, P043] |
| Robust optimiser | Protection against specified uncertainty/ambiguity | Can reduce nominal fragility | Ambiguity set arbitrary or blanket protection over-conservative | NO | Sensitivity, credible adverse scenarios, recourse policy | Robustness claim must state set, price and coverage boundary | [P044, P045] |
| Forecasting dashboard | Current decision-relevant predictive distribution and error | Supports staffing, inventory and timing decisions | Point forecasts hide calibration, shift and feedback; no downstream consumer | NO | Intervals, break-even bounds, simple combined forecast, direct trigger | Prediction must be evaluated through decision loss | [P046, P055] |
| AI/RL agent | State-contingent adaptive decision policy | May learn high-dimensional repeated policies | Reward/constraints invalid, unsafe exploration, weak external validity and no rollback | NO | Rules, bandits, rolling optimisation, human decision support | Domain translation, not evolved endpoint | [P047, P048, P062] |
| Digital twin or integrated enterprise model | Decision-relevant coupling and current state | Can coordinate strongly coupled systems and experiment safely | Opacity, stale interfaces, maintenance cost and no live owner | NO | Modular specialised models, interface budgets, decomposition | Integrate only when coupling value exceeds burden | [P050, P055, P064] |
| Safety stock formula | Reserve sized to demand/lead-time variability and shortage consequence | Protects service under uncertainty | Wrong demand/lead-time distribution, obsolete stock, hidden process failure | NO | Empirical quantiles, service simulation, explicit reserve policy | Buffer value is conditional, not universally good or bad | [P025, P035, P036] |
| Predictive-maintenance platform | Failure-state, observation and intervention policy | Can reduce failure/downtime when condition information is useful | Poor prognosis, common-cause failure, weak repair model, sensor and lifecycle costs | NO | Inspection rule, age replacement, run-to-failure for low consequence | Domain-specific and evidence-intensive | [P066] |

| TENSION | SIDE_A_PROPERTY | SIDE_B_PROPERTY | CONTEXT_THAT_FAVOURS_A | CONTEXT_THAT_FAVOURS_B | KNOWN_HYBRID_RESOLUTION | UNRESOLVED_RISK |

| Utilisation versus responsiveness | P022/P060: protect delay and reserve | P030/P037: avoid excessive idle resource cost | Variable demand, tail-sensitive service, recovery needs | Stable deterministic demand and expensive dedicated capacity | Service-level/cost frontier with reserve bands and admission control | Reserve sizing is assumption-sensitive |
| Slack versus resource cost | P025/P035: preserve recovery and option value | P036: count holding, delay and obsolescence cost | High variability, coupling and shortage consequence | Low variability, cheap rapid replenishment, perishable reserve | Consequence-sized reserve with periodic retirement | Buffers can hide process defects |
| Optimality versus robustness | P037/P039: exploit modelled opportunity | P044/P056: protect ambiguity and retain alternatives | Well-estimated stable model, reversible decision | Material ambiguity, tail/irreversible loss | Nominal/robust frontier with explicit price of robustness | Ambiguity-set calibration remains hard |
| Expected value versus tail consequence | P037: aggregate expected performance | P043: hard/tail/irreversible protection | Repeatable low-consequence outcomes | Catastrophic or non-compensatory consequence | Expected objective subject to tail/hard constraints | Rare-event probabilities may be unidentified |
| Efficiency versus resilience | P024/P037: reduce resource/cycle cost | P025/P042: reserve and recourse | Stable environment, easy recovery | Common-cause disruption, long recovery, high service consequence | Adaptive reserve plus tested recourse | Resilience value is difficult to monetise |
| Central optimisation versus local autonomy | P024/P064: coordinate externalities and shared bottlenecks | P019/P055: preserve local knowledge and authority | Strong coupling and shared constraints | Heterogeneous local information and fast adaptation | Hierarchical/decomposed model with controlled discretion | Central model may encode illegitimate authority |
| Schedule stability versus adaptive replanning | P033: reduce switching and coordination churn | P032/P047: respond to changed state | High switching/communication cost | Material failure, delay, priority or resource change | Event-triggered rolling horizon with frozen near-term window | Threshold can lag or oscillate |
| Model detail versus tractability | P011/P015: enough fidelity for consequence | P012/P037/P064: simple, timely and maintainable model | Close alternatives and material interactions | Cheap discriminator or large uncertainty dominates detail | Requisite modular modelling | Detail can create false confidence |
| Objective simplicity versus omitted externalities | P006/P037: clear operational target | P008/P053: affected-party and distributional consequence | Single legitimate owner and contained consequence | Cost shifting, fairness or environmental spillover | Hard externality constraints plus transparent primary objective | Stakeholder aggregation may lack authority |
| Deterministic commitment versus option preservation | P029/P033: stable execution and coordination | P009/P056: retain reversibility and alternatives | Low uncertainty and commitment enables value | High uncertainty, learning and irreversible downside | Stage-gated commitment with expiry and switch costs | Excessive flexibility can delay action |
| Sensitivity versus replanning churn | P016/P055: detect fragility and drift | P033/P049: avoid reacting to noise | High consequence and steep breakpoints | Noisy low-consequence fluctuations | Materiality bands, hysteresis and delayed review | False alarms versus stale model |
| Resource pooling versus common-mode coupling | P024/P028: share capacity and reduce fragmentation | P025/P043: isolate tail/common-cause failure | Independent demand and failure modes | Correlated demand/failure and shared bottleneck | Partial pooling plus protected reserve | Correlation can emerge under stress |
| Standardisation versus heterogeneous service/task distributions | P021/P026: comparable classes and policies | P027/P065: preserve heterogeneity and nonstationarity | Repeatable service classes | Knowledge work, learning, strategic arrivals | Class-based models plus empirical residual checks | Class definitions can be gamed |
| Robust conservatism versus opportunity cost | P044: protect against ambiguity | P037/P039: exploit expected opportunity | High downside and poorly identified uncertainty | Low consequence, reversible and data-rich decisions | Robustness-budget frontier and recourse | Worst-case set may be arbitrary |
| More information versus analysis latency | P013: acquire decision-changing evidence | P014/P012: act when ranking cannot materially change | High VOI, reversible delay and reusable learning | Deadline, low decision sensitivity, costly delay | Marginal decision-value stop/reopen rule | VOI estimate itself is uncertain |
| Exploration versus exploitation | P048: learn superior future policy | P043/P019: protect current consequence and authority | Repeated safe decisions with transferable learning | Irreversible or safety-critical exposure | Bounded pilots, safe exploration and offline evidence | Endogenous data can misprice exploration |
| Exact optimisation versus heuristic speed | P039: exploit formal bounds and exactness | P012/P037/P063: timely simple solution | High consequence, small gap matters, solve time available | Fast-changing state or large search space | Anytime/bounded heuristic with consequence-linked gap | Benchmark quality may not transfer |

| Forecast accuracy versus decision quality | P091-derived predictive calibration | P046/P054: downstream consequence | Prediction is direct decision objective | Asymmetric constraints and optimisation amplification | Evaluate both proper score and operational loss | Feedback can invalidate both |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_STRONGEST_SURVIVING_PROPERTIES
These properties have the strongest combination of historical provenance, formal logic, operational/implementation support and cross-domain transfer. Their artefact forms remain optional and their trigger/preconditions remain mandatory.

| Property | Failure prevented | Mature form | Evidence | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P001 — Explicit decision owner, consumer, deadline, and action authority | A model, dashboard, or recommendation has no live decision consumer, no deadline, or ambiguous authority, so analysis cannot control action legitimately. | Analysis begins with an owner-action-deadline tuple and ends in an implementable choice, deferment, experiment, policy, or documented non-decision. | formal=MODERATE; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=LOW | [S005, S006, S040, S073, S075, S076] |
| P002 — Frame the real decision and consequence before selecting a model | The model answers the wrong question, excludes important consequences, or treats a means/proxy as the end. | Model choice is downstream of a challengeable decision frame and can be changed without changing the underlying consequence statement. | formal=MODERATE; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=MODERATE | [S006, S040, S047, S071, S072, S073, S075] |
| P003 — Generate and preserve meaningful alternatives before ranking or optimisation | A precise ranking chooses the best member of an impoverished or politically pre-filtered set. | The decision set is treated as an engineered object with provenance, feasibility screening, dominance checks and a reopen rule. | formal=MODERATE; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=MODERATE | [S047, S074, S076, S035] |
| P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences | The solver returns a mathematically feasible but operationally impossible recommendation, or trades through a genuinely hard limit via a penalty. | Constraint status is challengeable and linked to enforcement, uncertainty, recourse and violation consequence; infeasibility is diagnostic, not proof that reality is impossible. | formal=HIGH; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=MODERATE | [S007, S010, S022, S073, S076, S062] |
| P006 — Trace objectives to consequences and resist proxy substitution | Metric improvement is reported as real improvement despite externalities, displaced cost, hidden queues, selection effects or changed behaviour. | A proxy remains provisional evidence about a consequence, with independent outcome validation and an explicit gaming/feedback model. | formal=MODERATE; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S006, S070, S105, S106, S107, S108] |
| P011 — Match model fidelity and analysis depth to decision consequence | Analysis costs and delays grow while added fidelity cannot change the next action, or a crude model is used where small errors reverse an irreversible choice. | Use the least-cost model that is adequate to discriminate the consequential decision, with a reopen rule when state or sensitivity changes. | formal=HIGH; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=MODERATE | [S043, S048, S049, S050, S073, S075] |
| P012 — Give cheap authoritative discriminators and simple heuristics precedence when sufficient | Complexity adds latency, maintenance and gaming surfaces without changing action or consequence. | Simple rules are preferred when validated for the context and monitored for drift; complexity is justified by incremental decision value, not prestige. | formal=HIGH; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S017, S043, S048, S049, S050, S073] |
| P015 — State model assumptions and validity domain as part of the decision claim | A valid calculation is transferred outside its stationarity, independence, causal, behavioural, distributional, or implementation domain. | Claims are scoped: optimal/valid under a stated representation and current evidence, with explicit transfer and drift limits. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S007, S027, S028, S084, S088, S089] |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | Small estimation, elicitation or normalisation changes reverse ranking, feasibility, priority or resource allocation. | Sensitivity is tied to whether action changes, not merely to output variance; unstable decisions trigger more information, robust options or preserved alternatives. | formal=HIGH; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S007, S025, S040, S041, S073, S083] |
| P018 — Separate solver or model optimality from real-decision validity | A provably optimal solution causes poor outcomes because the model is wrong, stale, local, unimplementable, or normatively defective. | No recommendation controls action solely because an optimiser converged; each validity layer has evidence and ownership. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S006, S007, S070, S084, S088, S098] |
| P019 — Establish implementation feasibility, operational authority, and usable decision support | The recommendation is ignored, selectively followed, worked around, or causes hidden operational damage. | Implementation is part of model validity; resistance can be evidence of missing constraints rather than a defect in users. | formal=LOW; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=MODERATE | [S073, S075, S076, S099, S100, S101, S102, S104] |
| P021 — Represent demand, arrivals, service, capacity, and variability before capacity claims | Average capacity appears sufficient but bursts or service variability produce long queues, loss, abandonment or missed deadlines. | Use the least-assumptive demand/capacity representation that discriminates overload, waiting and reserve decisions, with transient validation. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S001, S002, S014, S015, S016, S052, S056] |
| P022 — Govern utilisation jointly with waiting, congestion, and tail performance | Near-100% utilisation creates exploding delay, tail latency, abandonment, brittle recovery and hidden backlog. | Efficiency is assessed at system throughput and service consequence, not maximum busy fraction; controlled idle capacity can be rational. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S016, S051, S053, S054, S057] |
| P024 — Identify system bottlenecks and optimise end-to-end flow rather than local utilisation | Local optimisation creates excess WIP, starvation, blocking, retries or cost without increasing end-to-end throughput or consequence. | Capacity action is justified by marginal end-to-end consequence and accounts for bottleneck migration after intervention. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=MODERATE | [S009, S014, S017, S057] |
| P025 — Size capacity reserve and slack from variability, consequence, recovery, and coupling | System cannot absorb surge, failure, rework or recovery; or excess reserve imposes unjustified cost and hides problems. | Reserve is a priced hedge and recovery option, not waste or virtue; it is conditional, observable and periodically recalibrated. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S002, S051, S053, S057, S058] |
| P029 — Schedule parallel work from real precedence, resource, and acceptance conflicts | Unnecessary delay from false dependencies, or collision/rework from unsafe parallelism. | Parallelism is authorised by current conflict evidence and recomputed after state changes; neither issue-wide serialisation nor maximal concurrency is default. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S017, S018, S019, S061, S062, S064] |
| P032 — Recompute schedules and allocations after material state change | Resources follow a stale critical path or allocation while the actual bottleneck and feasible work have moved. | The schedule is a current decision policy with explicit recomputation and freeze/stability rules, not an archival chart. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S052, S053, S060, S063, S064, S112] |
| P041 — Distinguish variability, parameter uncertainty, ambiguity, model-form error, and nonstationarity | A method robust to sampled variability is claimed robust to misspecified models, structural breaks or unknown state spaces. | The uncertainty claim states what is known, estimated, bounded, disputed or unmodelled, and does not overgeneralise protection. | formal=HIGH; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=MODERATE; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S042, S044, S027, S028, S029, S086, S087] |
| P042 — Represent recourse and state-contingent corrective action | The model overstates downside by ignoring feasible correction or understates it by assuming unavailable recourse. | Robustness is achieved partly through credible recoverability, with recourse capacity and authority validated rather than assumed. | formal=HIGH; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S004, S020, S021, S022, S026, S030, S031, S127] |
| P043 — Treat tail, rare, irreversible, and high-consequence outcomes explicitly | An expected-optimal decision creates unacceptable catastrophic, tail-latency, shortage or safety exposure. | Tail protection is matched to consequence and evidence; probabilities and confidence levels are owned assumptions, not objective facts. | formal=HIGH; empirical=MODERATE; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S022, S032, S045, S054, S075] |
| P050 — Verify implementation and validate simulation against its decision purpose | A simulation faithfully executes the wrong logic, fits history for the wrong reasons, or is reused outside its validated domain. | A simulation has a bounded credibility claim tied to a decision, state, data regime and consequence—not a certificate that the model is true. | formal=MODERATE; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S084, S088, S089, S090] |
| P053 — Detect and resist objective, constraint, data, queue, and reporting gaming | The optimisation surface improves while real consequence worsens; post-hoc model revision makes a preferred alternative appear optimal. | Targets are treated as interventions in a socio-technical system, with protected provenance and independent consequences that can invalidate the metric. | formal=MODERATE; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S105, S106, S107, S108, S109, S110, S096, S097] |
| P055 — Monitor realised consequences and retire or revise models after drift | Drift, changed incentives, altered service processes or new constraints silently invalidate the decision logic; failure is blamed on execution without testing the model. | Validity is time-bounded and consequence-tested; a model remains authoritative only while owned evidence supports its current decision use. | formal=MODERATE; empirical=HIGH; field=HIGH; implementation=HIGH; transfer=HIGH; assumption_sensitivity=HIGH | [S063, S070, S093, S096, S097, S100, S101, S104, S124] |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_CONTEXT_SPECIFIC_PROPERTIES
| Property | Why context-specific | Trigger | Non-trigger/cheap path | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P026 — Make admission, priority, and service discipline explicit | Parametric queue models can be powerful within domain but are brittle under heterogeneous, strategic, nonstationary, or feedback-coupled work; qualitative congestion properties transfer more widely than distributions. | Overload, heterogeneous consequences, deadlines, finite capacity, competing classes or safety/mission priorities. | Use a transparent priority/ageing rule with explicit exceptions; avoid queueing optimisation when consequences clearly order work. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT |
| P033 — Balance schedule stability against adaptive replanning and switching costs | Optimal schedules are often fragile to duration and availability error; schedule stability and implementability can dominate nominal makespan. | Recurring rescheduling with setup, context-switch, commitment or coordination costs. | Use a minimum-improvement threshold and protect near-term committed work unless safety or feasibility changes. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT |
| P034 — Use work-conserving execution only within conflict, option, safety, and congestion bounds | Optimal schedules are often fragile to duration and availability error; schedule stability and implementability can dominate nominal makespan. | Ready work exists but starting it could create shared-resource conflict, WIP, lock-in, setup, safety or priority harm. | Start the highest-value conflict-free work; remain idle when no eligible work has positive net consequence. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT |
| P036 — Choose service-level, shortage, backorder, and holding trade-offs explicitly | Buffer value is context-specific; excessive reserve can increase cost, obsolescence, delay, moral hazard, and hidden WIP. | Inventory, staffing or reserve choices with explicit service or shortage consequence. | Use a policy threshold from authoritative service requirement and observed variability; do not estimate a full cost curve when not identifiable. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT |
| P039 — Interpret solver tolerances and optimality gaps through real-world regret | Formal optimality is conditional on the model; small optimality gaps can coexist with large real-world regret, and more exact algorithms do not repair misspecification. | Large/exact optimisation, close alternatives, numerically sensitive constraints, binary thresholds or costly solve time. | Check whether the incumbent and bound imply different real actions; stop if not and model uncertainty dominates. | ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE |
| P040 — Use dual values and shadow prices as model-relative marginal signals | Formal optimality is conditional on the model; small optimality gaps can coexist with large real-world regret, and more exact algorithms do not repair misspecification. | Resource allocation models with meaningful and stable constraints where marginal analysis could guide capacity or prioritisation. | Inspect binding constraints and perform a small finite change scenario rather than treating an infinitesimal dual as truth. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT |
| P048 — Trade learning and exploration against operating consequence and information value | Formal regret or policy guarantees are environment- and model-dependent; reinforcement learning is one translation, not the universal endpoint. | Repeated decisions with material uncertainty, learnable response, future reuse and safe/reversible experimentation. | Use historical/offline evidence, a deterministic discriminator, or a small controlled pilot when full adaptive exploration is unnecessary or unsafe. | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT |
| P054 — Validate data-driven and decision-focused models in the deployed decision loop | Decision-focused learning and RL can improve formal downstream loss under benchmark assumptions, but current external-validity, safety, scalability and implementation evidence remains uneven. | Learned predictions, costs, constraints, policies or surrogate solvers materially control operational decisions. | Prefer a transparent calibrated predictor plus robust/simple decision rule when end-to-end learning has no demonstrated incremental decision value. | ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVE |
| P062 — Reinforcement learning is a domain translation, not the evolved endpoint | The named practice may still be useful in a bounded context; rejection applies to its elevation into a universal property. | Repeated high-dimensional sequential decisions where interaction data, safe learning and demonstrable policy advantage exist. | Use a rule, bandit, rolling optimiser, supervised forecast plus policy, or human-in-the-loop decision support when these settle the operational need. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC |
| P063 — Metaheuristics are conditional search techniques, not universal engineering properties | The named practice may still be useful in a bounded context; rejection applies to its elevation into a universal property. | Well-specified hard search problems where exact optimisation is too costly and approximate solution quality affects consequence materially. | Use domain heuristics, decomposition, greedy/list scheduling or a solver with an optimality gap where sufficient. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC |
| P064 — A giant integrated model is useful only when integration value exceeds opacity and maintenance cost | Adoption is not proof of validity and resistance is not proof of irrationality; implementation can reveal missing constraints or conflicting objectives. | Strong cross-system coupling where local decisions materially externalise cost and a shared model can be maintained and governed. | Coordinate a few binding interfaces, budgets or bottlenecks between smaller models rather than build an all-encompassing digital representation. | USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_BUREAUCRATISED |
| P065 — Universal transfer of parametric queue, inventory, and scheduling formulas to knowledge or agent work remains unresolved | The named practice may still be useful in a bounded context; rejection applies to its elevation into a universal property. | Novel service, software, knowledge or agentic systems where queue/capacity/schedule effects are plausible but the stochastic process is not established. | Use direct WIP/backlog, elapsed-time, bottleneck and conflict observations; avoid distributional formulas until diagnostics support them. | UNRESOLVED |
| P066 — Use maintenance and replacement policies only with a credible failure-state and renewal model | Formal regret or policy guarantees are environment- and model-dependent; reinforcement learning is one translation, not the universal endpoint. | Assets or services with material failure consequence, repeated life cycles, observable condition or age dependence, and controllable maintenance/replacement action. | Use manufacturer/field failure evidence, a conservative inspection interval, direct condition threshold or run-to-failure where consequence is low and replacement is cheap; avoid predictive optimisation without incremental value. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_REJECTED_OR_SUPERSEDED_PRACTICES
| Property/candidate | Disposition | What survives | Why rejected/superseded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P057 — A named solver or optimisation algorithm is not a universal engineering property | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | No solver family is admitted as a general property; the surviving property is fit-for-decision computation under verified formulation and bounded cost. | A wrong objective, missing alternative, invalid distribution or infeasible implementation is solved faster or more exactly without improving the real decision. |
| P058 — A fixed deterministic PERT/CPM/Gantt network is superseded as general schedule authority | SUPERSEDED_BY_STRONGER_FORM | Precedence and schedule-critical constraints are retained; the fixed chart as future truth is rejected. | Published critical paths become stale; nominal parallelism is resource-infeasible; padded estimates and independence assumptions produce false confidence. |
| P059 — A universal weighted scorecard is rejected as an objective ranking mechanism | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | Explicit challengeable trade-offs survive; a universal weighted scorecard does not. | A preferred result is manufactured through post-hoc weights, bounds or criteria while numerical totals obscure value conflict and fragility. |
| P060 — One-hundred-percent utilisation as an efficiency target is rejected | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | Idle capacity can be an option and congestion-control resource; its value is consequence- and variability-dependent. | Near saturation causes explosive waiting, abandonment, backlog, missed deadlines and no room for surge or maintenance; local busy-ness degrades system throughput. |
| P061 — Simulation run count is not a general credibility property | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | Runs buy only a bounded reduction in simulation sampling error; they do not validate the world model. | Extremely precise estimates are produced for an invalid model, wrong horizon, biased initial state or narrow scenario set. |

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_CURRENT_STATE_AND_RESEARCH_FRONTIER
As of 12 August 2026, the frontier is active but does not overturn the mature boundaries above. Current work is expanding formal capability while also making uncertainty, feedback and implementation burdens more explicit.

| Frontier | Formal/current advance | Engineering evidence limit | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Distributionally robust optimisation | Finite-sample/statistical guarantees, multimodal and decision-dependent uncertainty, learned ambiguity sets. | Ambiguity-set choice, decision-induced shift, tractability and prospective field calibration remain open. | [S029, S120, S121] |
| Decision-focused learning | Training and evaluation against downstream optimisation loss rather than prediction score alone. | External validity, endogeneity, feedback, constraint correctness, prospective comparison and implementation evidence remain uneven. | [S067, S068, S069, S096, S097] |
| Probabilistic and judgmental forecasting | Decision-focused pooling, operational profit tests, forecast combination and structural-break handling. | Better forecast metrics do not guarantee decision value; adjustment incentives and regime change remain consequential. | [S092, S093, S094, S095, S115, S124] |
| Online and learning-augmented optimisation | Policies with switching costs, cross-level constraints and untrusted predictions. | Adversarial robustness, delayed/partial observation, implementation latency and authority are still assumption-sensitive. | [S112, S119] |
| Safe reinforcement learning | Constraint, risk and safe-exploration formulations. | Safety specification, scalability, generalisation, reward validity and field replication remain major limits. | [S117, S118] |
| Queueing for software, compute and LLM systems | Modern workload, prediction and service-system formulations. | Service definitions, nonstationarity, feedback, retries and transfer from classical queues remain unresolved. | [S055, S113] |
| Simulation methodology | Input/parameter uncertainty, output analysis, simulation optimisation and designed evidence. | Model-form uncertainty and decision-purpose validation still dominate run-count ritual. | [S087, S111] |
| Maintenance optimisation | Condition information, multi-component coupling, joint maintenance/operations and partially observed policies. | Failure-state identification, prognosis, repair effectiveness and lifecycle cost limit transfer. | [S131, S132] |
| OR discipline and AI integration | Plural method portfolio, AI complementarity, problem formulation and implementation research. | Practice incentives, adoption, human expertise and organisational authority remain explicit frontier concerns. | [S071, S101, S102, S103] |

**Evidence disposition.** These sources establish a current research frontier. They do not justify a claim that DRO, DFL, RL, predictive maintenance, digital twins or AI–OR integration is the universal mature form.

## EVOLVED_DECISION_AND_OPERATIONS_ENGINEERING_OPEN_QUESTIONS
**Cross-family unresolved questions**

- How can decision-frame completeness be bounded when the feasible design space and stakeholder set are open-ended?
- What operational tests best distinguish proxy improvement from consequence improvement after behaviour adapts?
- How should ambiguity sets and robustness budgets be calibrated under decision-dependent or structural distribution change?
- When does another simulation/model refinement have greater expected decision value than a field experiment, pilot or direct discriminator?
- What empirical signatures justify queueing and scheduling abstractions for heterogeneous human–AI work?
- How can common-cause failure be represented when it disables both primary capacity and assumed recourse?
- What prospective study designs identify the incremental field value of decision-focused learning over transparent predict-then-optimise baselines?
- Which domains have replicated evidence that RL outperforms simpler governed policies after safety, monitoring and implementation cost?
- How should near-optimality tolerance be connected to real consequence and model uncertainty rather than a percentage of a proxy objective?
- How can stakeholder disagreement be preserved when no legitimate common utility or fairness criterion exists?
- How should schedule-replan thresholds balance currentness against coordination and switching churn?
- When does central integration prevent harmful local optimisation, and when does it create opacity and illegitimate authority?
- What independent outcome remains measurable after a target or model changes the data-generating process?
- When does predictive/condition-based maintenance outperform simple age, inspection or run-to-failure rules after full sensing and lifecycle cost?
- How should evidence strength be updated after implementation failures that could arise from model, data, authority, incentives or execution?

**Property-specific open questions**

| Property | Open question(s) |
| --- | --- |
| P001 — Explicit decision owner, consumer, deadline, and action authority | How should authority be represented when consequences and control are distributed across organisations? |
| P002 — Frame the real decision and consequence before selecting a model | How much stakeholder participation is required before a frame is legitimate in distributed systems? |
| P003 — Generate and preserve meaningful alternatives before ranking or optimisation | How can alternative-generation completeness be bounded without pretending the design space is enumerable? |
| P004 — Include status quo, no-action, deferment, and staged commitment where feasible | When do organisational commitments make a nominal no-action option infeasible in practice? |
| P005 — Distinguish feasible alternatives, enforceable hard constraints, and soft preferences | How should contested legal, ethical or policy constraints be represented without laundering them into coefficients? |
| P006 — Trace objectives to consequences and resist proxy substitution | What independent outcomes remain observable after optimisation changes the data-generating process? |
| P007 — Preserve multiple objectives, Pareto structure, and non-compensatory limits | How should irreducible stakeholder disagreement be represented when no legitimate common utility exists? |
| P008 — Represent stakeholders, distributional effects, fairness, and externalities | Which fairness or externality constraints have legitimate authority in plural-stakeholder settings? |
| P009 — Account for reversibility, irreversibility, option value, and staged commitment | How should option value be bounded where future alternatives are endogenous and probabilities are unidentified? |
| P010 — Represent decision horizon, dependencies, and sequential coupling | What horizon is sufficient when distant consequences are uncertain but potentially irreversible? |
| P011 — Match model fidelity and analysis depth to decision consequence | How should adequacy be tested when several stakeholders have different loss functions? |
| P012 — Give cheap authoritative discriminators and simple heuristics precedence when sufficient | What evidence is sufficient to validate a heuristic under drift and adversarial incentives? |
| P013 — Bound information, analysis, and computation by expected decision value | How should qualitative VOI be governed when probabilities, utilities or model classes are disputed? |
| P014 — Use explicit stop and reopen rules tied to possible action change | How should reopening thresholds avoid both inertia and replanning churn? |
| P015 — State model assumptions and validity domain as part of the decision claim | Which model assumptions require empirical validation versus merely transparent disclosure? |
| P016 — Test sensitivity to parameters, probabilities, weights, and modelling choices | How should correlated model-form choices be explored without combinatorial scenario theatre? |
| P017 — Correct for optimiser's curse and validate out-of-sample decision performance | Which out-of-sample design is valid when decisions change the future data distribution? |
| P018 — Separate solver or model optimality from real-decision validity | What minimum end-to-end evidence is required before automated optimiser output may directly control action? |
| P019 — Establish implementation feasibility, operational authority, and usable decision support | How should override rights be calibrated so that local knowledge is preserved without defeating valid constraints? |
| P020 — Retire or rebuild stale models, schedules, forecasts, and metrics without a live consumer | What drift indicators best predict decision invalidity rather than harmless input movement? |
| P021 — Represent demand, arrivals, service, capacity, and variability before capacity claims | Which empirical abstractions are adequate for heterogeneous knowledge and agent work? |
| P022 — Govern utilisation jointly with waiting, congestion, and tail performance | How should tail and fairness costs be combined when capacity serves heterogeneous classes? |
| P023 — Make queues, WIP, backlogs, blocking, and ageing visible | How should partially observed or strategically hidden queues be estimated? |
| P024 — Identify system bottlenecks and optimise end-to-end flow rather than local utilisation | How should moving and endogenous bottlenecks be governed under adaptive demand? |
| P025 — Size capacity reserve and slack from variability, consequence, recovery, and coupling | How should correlated common-mode failures be reflected without extreme conservatism? |
| P026 — Make admission, priority, and service discipline explicit | What priority/fairness rules remain legitimate when stakeholder utilities are incomparable? |
| P027 — Distinguish transient, nonstationary, overloaded, and feedback-congested regimes | How should feedback from adaptive users and automated retries be identified in partially observed systems? |
| P028 — Model queue networks, shared bottlenecks, retries, rework, and blocking when coupled | What minimal network abstraction preserves fork-join and shared-acceptance delay in agentic systems? |
| P029 — Schedule parallel work from real precedence, resource, and acceptance conflicts | How should acceptance and information-conflict resources be represented when they are not conventional machines? |
| P030 — Treat resource ceilings as constraints, not utilisation targets | When should unused capacity trigger investigation versus be accepted as rational reserve? |
| P031 — Represent uncertain duration, release, setup, blocking, and deadline structure | Which duration distributions, if any, are defensible for novel knowledge work? |
| P032 — Recompute schedules and allocations after material state change | Which triggers minimise stale-plan loss without inducing excessive replanning churn? |
| P033 — Balance schedule stability against adaptive replanning and switching costs | How should cognitive and trust costs of schedule changes be measured? |
| P034 — Use work-conserving execution only within conflict, option, safety, and congestion bounds | What minimal eligibility model prevents premature work without recreating a heavy scheduler? |
| P035 — Value inventory, buffers, slack, and reserve conditionally rather than categorically | How should information and attention buffers be valued in non-repeatable work? |
| P036 — Choose service-level, shortage, backorder, and holding trade-offs explicitly | How should rare catastrophic shortages be combined with routine service economics? |
| P037 — Use mathematical optimisation only when decision complexity and value warrant it | How should expected implementation benefit be estimated before building the model? |
| P038 — Treat formulation, infeasibility, and implementability as diagnostics | How should conflict diagnosis be prioritised when hundreds of policy constraints are contested? |
| P039 — Interpret solver tolerances and optimality gaps through real-world regret | How can real-regret bounds be constructed when the objective is a contested proxy? |
| P040 — Use dual values and shadow prices as model-relative marginal signals | When do discrete or strategic responses invalidate marginal capacity values? |
| P041 — Distinguish variability, parameter uncertainty, ambiguity, model-form error, and nonstationarity | How can deep/model uncertainty be operationalised without arbitrary ambiguity sets? |
| P042 — Represent recourse and state-contingent corrective action | How should common-mode failures that disable several recourse options be represented? |
| P043 — Treat tail, rare, irreversible, and high-consequence outcomes explicitly | How should rare-event probabilities be bounded where historical data are structurally sparse? |
| P044 — Calibrate robustness to credible ambiguity rather than blanket conservatism | How can ambiguity-set calibration be validated under decision-induced distribution shift? |
| P045 — Use scenarios and stress tests without claiming future-event completeness | What evidence supports scenario-set adequacy under deep uncertainty? |
| P046 — Carry forecast uncertainty and decision loss into operational choices | Which predictive improvements retain value after optimisation, operator adjustment and regime change? |
| P047 — Use state-contingent policies and rolling re-optimisation for revisable decisions | What event threshold best balances responsiveness against replanning churn and implementation instability? |
| P048 — Trade learning and exploration against operating consequence and information value | How should exploration be valued when data are endogenous and harmful outcomes are irreversible? |
| P049 — Represent delayed and partial feedback, switching cost, lock-in, and hysteresis | How can delayed causal effects be separated from ordinary operational noise under adaptive policy? |
| P050 — Verify implementation and validate simulation against its decision purpose | What external validation is feasible for one-off systems or interventions with no close historical analogue? |
| P051 — Control replications, transients, dependence, and input uncertainty in simulation evidence | How should simulation budgets be allocated between replication, input learning and alternative model forms? |
| P052 — Test multi-criteria rankings against weights, scales, normalisation, thresholds, and method choice | When stakeholder utilities cannot be legitimately aggregated, which partial-order or deliberative output should control action? |
| P053 — Detect and resist objective, constraint, data, queue, and reporting gaming | How can model governance detect strategic omissions when the evaluator and decision owner share incentives? |
| P054 — Validate data-driven and decision-focused models in the deployed decision loop | Which prospective evaluation designs identify decision benefit when deployment changes the data-generating process? |
| P055 — Monitor realised consequences and retire or revise models after drift | How quickly can drift be distinguished from noise without causing excessive model or schedule churn? |
| P056 — Preserve near-optimal alternatives and portfolios when model discrimination is weak | How should an epsilon for ‘near-optimal’ be tied to consequence and model uncertainty rather than arbitrary percentage? |
| P057 — A named solver or optimisation algorithm is not a universal engineering property | Which solver-level diagnostics most effectively expose formulation defects rather than merely numerical difficulty? |
| P058 — A fixed deterministic PERT/CPM/Gantt network is superseded as general schedule authority | Which uncertainty and resource representations produce enough schedule improvement to justify their maintenance cost in small projects? |
| P059 — A universal weighted scorecard is rejected as an objective ranking mechanism | What minimum sensitivity disclosure should accompany any public or high-stakes weighted ranking? |
| P060 — One-hundred-percent utilisation as an efficiency target is rejected | How should reserve targets be estimated for bursty, strategic or human work with changing service distributions? |
| P061 — Simulation run count is not a general credibility property | Can practical stopping rules jointly allocate effort across replication and structural-model challenge? |
| P062 — Reinforcement learning is a domain translation, not the evolved endpoint | Which operational domains have replicated field evidence that RL outperforms simpler governed policies after full implementation cost? |
| P063 — Metaheuristics are conditional search techniques, not universal engineering properties | What minimum baseline and reproducibility standard should govern field claims for metaheuristic superiority? |
| P064 — A giant integrated model is useful only when integration value exceeds opacity and maintenance cost | How can the marginal value of integration be measured before incurring irreversible model-maintenance cost? |
| P065 — Universal transfer of parametric queue, inventory, and scheduling formulas to knowledge or agent work remains unresolved | Which empirical signatures justify particular queueing or scheduling abstractions for heterogeneous human–AI work?; How should endogenous task generation and shared validation resources be represented? |
| P066 — Use maintenance and replacement policies only with a credible failure-state and renewal model | How transferable are learned condition thresholds across operating regimes and maintenance organisations?; When does predictive maintenance outperform simple age/inspection rules after sensing and model-lifecycle cost? |
